title: Israel's Netanyahu addresses U.N. as many leaders walk out
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu focused on Iran, and on defending Israel's actions in Gaza and the West Bank amid condemnation from fellow leaders at the U.N.
story: Tel Aviv — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday as his country faces broad condemnation and growing isolation over Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip and the occupied West Bank.
As Netanyahu took the stage, many attendees walked out.
"If there are any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall, please do so now," Netanyahu began.
Netanyahu arrived in New York early Thursday morning and is due to leave just a few hours after his speech.
Leaders from Europe and the Middle East, including France, the U.K., Jordan, Syria, Qatar and Turkey, devoted at least some of their time at the U.N. podium Wednesday to harshly denounce Israel.

Analysts expected Netanyahu would take advantage of the critical focus on Israel to demonstrate his ability to defend his country on the international stage just weeks before a tightly contested Israeli election.

It's an unusually brief trip to New York for Netanyahu during the General Assembly. He has often capitalized on the autumn visits to meet with other world leaders, particularly the American president and secretary of state.
Referring to the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack carried out by Hamas, Netanyahu said that instead of collapsing, "we rose and fought like lions."
"With our great American friends, we crushed Iran's army, navy, air force and nuclear facilities," he said, later thanking President Trump for his "bold leadership."
"We will continue to defend our state. We will continue to win because we have no other choice," he said.

His office said he would meet Thursday with the presidents of Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Panama and Ethiopia, the vice president of Colombia, and the prime ministers of Greece, Slovenia, and Papua New Guinea. He is not due to meet with Mr. Trump.
Netanyahu's office said this year's trip would be so brief because the prime minister needs to return to Israel for the Jewish holiday of Sukkot, which begins Friday evening.

In his speech, Netanyahu was expected to focus primarily on Iran, according to a person familiar with the matter. He will also likely defend Israel's ongoing military campaigns in Gaza and in neighboring countries such as Syria.
Netanyahu has used past General Assembly addresses to make claims about Iran's military and nuclear efforts, and he has promised surprises in his upcoming speeches.
Netanyahu's beef with Mamdani
Netanyahu also vowed to respond in his U.N. address to the latest criticism from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

In a video responding to Mamdani calling him a "war criminal" earlier this week, Netanyahu said he would use his speech at the U.N. to "tell the truth about" the mayor, whom he accused of supporting Hamas.
Netanyahu's response came nearly 30 minutes into his address, where he accused Mamdani of spreading "lies" about Jews and called him "antisemitic."
"Shame on you," Netanyahu said. "Shame on you for distorting the facts, shame on you for inverting victim and aggressor, shame on you for spitting in the face of truth."

"You falsely, repeatedly accuse Israel of genocide," he continued. "You try to stop me from coming here. You try to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth. Here's a simple truth: Israel didn't commit genocide. Israel prevented genocide."

During his election campaign, Mamdani had threatened to have New York authorities act on an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court for Netanyahu, should he attend the U.N. gathering.

The mayor later recognized that he couldn't have Netanyahu detained, but he urged federal U.S. authorities to detain him instead and noted that New Yorkers would still have an outlet to express their feelings about the Israeli leader, calling the act of protest "one of the bedrocks of our city."

Nearly two dozen were taken into police custody in protests in New York on Thursday, including of Mamdani's ally, House Democratic nominee Darializa Avila Chevalier. Netanyahu rebuked the planned protests in a video earlier this week.
"Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews. I'm coming to the U.N. I'm going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell the truth about you," Netanyahu said.
Condemnation of Israel, and Israeli pushback
Netanyahu spoke after a spate of speeches condemning his government's policies.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the leaders gathered at the U.N. on Wednesday that while Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, terror attack on Israel was "utterly horrific," the scale of the Israeli response has been unjustified.

"Far too many people have died — including so many children. Far too little aid is getting in, and it has gone on for far too long," Burnham said of Gaza, where Israeli forces have occupied more than half of the Palestinian territory since the war with Hamas.
The speech by France's President Emmanuel Macron sparked ire in Israel after he accused the country of daily violations in the other Palestinian territory, the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

"Look at what is happening in West Bank, where there are violations every day. In the name of what? Hamas has never struck in the West Bank," said the French leader. "This every day makes it more impossible to achieve respect for the Palestinian people's legitimate right to exist."

Netanyahu called Macron's statement about Hamas a "grotesque absurdity," noting that on Sunday, French citizen and father of six Netanel Shukrun was killed in an attack that Netanyahu said was carried out by a Hamas terrorist.
Hamas issued a statement praising the attack, but it did not claim responsibility.

The group, long designated a terrorist organization by the U.S., Israel and the European Union, has not been part of the Palestinian administration in the West Bank since 2007. It has, however, maintained its own militant network in the West Bank for decades, according to Israeli and Palestinian officials.

"Hamas terrorists carry out attacks against Jews almost every day. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu added Wednesday, using the official Israeli name for the West Bank.

King Abdullah of Jordan, which signed a peace agreement decades ago with Israel, told the U.N. on Wednesday that Israel should be hit with sanctions, asset freezes, embargoes and diplomatic isolation.

Spencer wrote that he believed the diatribe was the result of Charles’ "pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death."
After the excerpt from the book was released last week, Buckingham Palace issued a rare statement.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said.

Spencer wrote that after falling in love with heart surgeon Dr. Hasnat Khan following her divorce, Diana had the "naïve yet impossible" dream of moving to South Africa — where Spencer lived at the time — with her boyfriend because England had become "intolerable" to her.

But for Glanville, the financial fallout from her health battle has been just as daunting as the physical toll.

"The medical system here is broken," Glanville explained. "So I have, like, from 8 a.m. on, I have creditors from, like, medical things calling me, like from Cedars-Sinai. It's out of control. Like I spent hundreds of thousands of dollars that I had saved. I emptied my 401(k). And it's all for medical bills. And I had insurance, and they told me nothing was wrong. I'm so angry. Jeff Garlin is opening up about his contentious exit from "The Goldbergs," saying his undiagnosed bipolar disorder contributed to the behavior that strained relationships with his co-stars before he left the hit sitcom.

The 64-year-old actor starred as the Goldbergs' family patriarch, Murray Goldberg, on the show from its premiere in September 2013 until he departed the ABC show during its ninth season in December 2021 amid HR investigations into complaints about his on-set behavior.

Garlin was accused by members of the cast and crew of inappropriate verbal conduct, unwanted physical contact, including hugging and touching, and behavior that some employees described as creating an uncomfortable work environment.
JEFF GARLIN DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM CANCEL CULTURE AMID ‘THE GOLDBERGS’ ON-SET CONDUCT ALLEGATIONS

While speaking with Vanity Fair at the time, Garlin denied intentionally harassing anyone. He acknowledged that HR had spoken to him over several years but characterized the complaints as stemming from his style of comedy and "silliness" on set rather than malicious intent.
He also said he was willing to adjust behaviors, like no longer hugging people.

Wendi McLendon-Covey is pushing back on her former "The Goldbergs" star Jeff Garlin's claims about his on-set behavior. (Noel Vasquez/Getty Images; Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for International Myeloma Foundation)

During a March 2023 appearance on SiriusXM's "Andy Cohen Live," Garlin's co-star, Wendi McLendon-Covey, who played his wife Beverly Goldberg on "The Goldbergs," said his exit was "a long time coming" and that "finally, someone is listening to us." She declined to discuss the situation further, saying she was "exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all."

On Monday, Garlin appeared on the Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast and addressed McLendon-Covey's comments and attributed his behavior to a mental health condition that had not been diagnosed at the time.

"It wasn't a long time coming for me," he said in reference to McLendon-Covey's past remark. "I actually empathize with her because, at the time, I was undiagnosed bipolar, and I was miserable on the show.

"I was miserable with my performance," he continued. "She was always trying to tell me, 'Hey, you're really great on the show.' I didn't believe her, and I just got to the point where I had to quit. She was very resentful, and it was a bit dramatic.

"I can only speak to what I'm responsible for," Garlin added. "Being bipolar, I was either one of three things: dark, dark, dark — where I didn't talk or look at anyone — happy to the point of mania, never turning off my thing or mean, really, really mean. I didn't know which one I was going to be. I didn't get diagnosed until I was 59. This was toward the end of my time on ‘The Goldbergs,’ so I could be a lot.
'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WAS LOCKED IN PSYCH WARD AS HEALTH BATTLE SPIRALED

"When I left, she was very resentful and angry at me. If she wants to continue the resentment, that's her. I don't have resentment toward her, even for saying things about me. I actually love her, and I appreciate that she's one of the greatest actors I've ever worked with. And that will not be lost on me."
Garlin left the show during its ninth season in 2021. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
McLendon-Covey, 56, responded to Garlin's comments after the Daily Beast shared a clip from his interview on Instagram.
"Huh," she wrote in the comments section.

After an Instagram user asked her, "What’s your take, Wendi?," the "Bridesmaids" star wrote, "Let's just say I remember things very differently, as does the crew, the other actors, the writers and our executives."
Fox News Digital has reached out to representatives for Garlin and McLendon-Covey for comment.
Garlin said his on-set behavior was fueled by undiagnosed bipolar disorder.  (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
"The Goldbergs" followed the misadventures of a loud but loving family living in suburban Philadelphia during the 1980s.

Though Garlin left "The Goldbergs" during its ninth season, he was a regular cast member for part of that season. After his exit, the show completed some remaining Season 9 episodes using previously filmed footage and stand-ins before writing Murray Goldberg out ahead of Season 10. At the beginning of the tenth season, the show revealed that the character had died off-screen, allowing the series to continue focusing on the Goldberg family without him.
ABC announced in February 2023 that Season 10 would be the show's last, and the series finale aired on May 3, 2023.

While appearing on the "Obsessed" podcast, Garlin reflected on how his life and career had changed since he was diagnosed with bipolar disorder.
McLendon-Covey disputed his account on social media.  (ABC via Getty Images)

"It's changed quite a bit because, A, I went into AA (Acloholics Anonymous)," he said. "B, I had a nervous breakdown right after that as the ‘The Goldbergs’ thing was ending. I had a nervous breakdown, was suicidal. Went away. Learned this kind of therapy. Got the right drugs in me. The right cocktail, as they say, for bipolar. And I got a form of therapy that was new to me, called Dialectical Behavior Therapy. DBT.

"So, you know, I have regrets," he continued. "Not a lot of them that I could have controlled, but I still have regrets on a lot of my behavior in terms of being a jerk. But I'm really a different person.

"No, I'm the same person," Garlin clarified. "I'm more enlightened.
The two played husband and wife on the hit sitcom.  (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

"Like I said, I don't have resentments," he added. "When I have a resentment, I work through it on my own until it doesn't help me any. I'm sober. I'm grateful. I was never grateful for my time on ‘The Goldbergs.’ That was another problem. ‘I’m not grateful for this great opportunity?' No, I wasn't. And now I'm grateful for everything, and so it has changed me.

"I'm still the same person at heart because I always — I would leave the set thinking, ‘Why did I apologize to a lot of people today?’ Having no idea. Because in my heart now, and logically, I know I'm good-hearted, but I wasn't able to — I was misguided. I don't know. But the point is, I'm really grateful for what I have now and the way I am now."

title: Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium concerts called off as troubled tour faces fresh setback
summary: Severe weather warnings forced Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows to be canceled amid a backdrop of controversy involving Macklemore and Robert Kraft.
story: Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo discusses a fight that broke out on a flight to London and the controversy surrounding Ed Sheeran after Macklemore was dropped from his tour on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’
Ed Sheeran's concerts at Gillette Stadium have been canceled.

Sheeran was set to perform at the Foxborough, Massachusetts, venue on Sept. 25 and 26, but according to a statement shared on social media, potentially dangerous weather conditions have forced the singer to step back.

"Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," Sheeran's tour promoter, Messina Touring Group, said in a statement. "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority."
ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS
Ed Sheeran's shows at Gillette Stadium have been canceled. (Deadline via Getty Images)
The company noted that refunds are available at the point of purchase. Gillette Stadium reposted the statement.

While the weather prompted the cancellations, the owner of Gillette Stadium, Robert Kraft, has been in the headlines recently due to the controversy surrounding Sheeran and one of the former openers for his tour, Macklemore.

After Macklemore used his slot at Sheeran's MetLife Stadium shows to express his support for Palestinians, many people were upset, including owners of stadiums where Sheeran was slated to play. The "Thrift Shop" rapper was eventually dropped from the tour, and in a lengthy statement reacting to the news, he wrote in part, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran's tour after using his set to speak about his political views. (Redferns)

Kraft then issued a statement of his own that read, "Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech."

"Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The statement continued, "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike."
Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium, has said that he's a fan of Sheeran. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images)

Kraft wrote that he agreed with Macklemore that "too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering," but argued that "only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate."
He added, "Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Kraft shared that he's spent a considerable amount of time in recent years "focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed."

He has a "tremendous respect" for Sheeran and his music, Kraft explained, and he said that he'd also be happy to speak personally with Macklemore, "because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."
WATCH: ED SHEERAN CALLED OUT FOR CAVING TO ANTI-ISRAEL MOB
While it's not clear if Macklemore has pursued that opportunity, he did announce this week that in October, he's headed to Europe for a set of shows he's calling the "Free Palestine Tour."
Despite the promoter saying severe weather forced the cancellation of Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, several people shared other theories on social media.
"Mother Nature really said ‘not in Kraft’s house,'" one person wrote.
Sheeran's opening acts have backed out of the tour following Macklemore's exit. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for iHeartRadio)
Another joked, "The bad weather being refunds and public backlash."

It's unclear if the shows will be rescheduled.

title: '80s star Tiffany steps into dream role after leaving Hollywood behind
summary: Tiffany reveals her Off-Broadway role in "Spandex the Musical" fulfills a lifelong dream she put on hold when "I Think We're Alone Now" took off.
story: Tiffany Darwish told Fox News Digital that by 6 PM everyday, she is in the kitchen cooking before a peaceful night.
'80s pop icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight as she fulfills a dream she had prior to becoming a teen idol.
The 54-year-old singer, who rose to fame in 1987 after her song "I Think We're Alone Now" became a massive hit, made her Off-Broadway debut in "Spandex the Musical" last week.
During a July interview with People magazine, Tiffany reflected on why taking the stage felt like a "true full-circle moment for me."
'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD
"Before music came into my life, I was a dancer and an actor, and those dreams were put on hold when ‘I Think We’re Alone Now’ took off and my recording career began," she said.
'80s icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight to fulfill her lifelong dream after leaving Hollywood. (Bruce Glikas/Getty Images; Frank Hempel/United Archives via Getty Images)

Tiffany, whose full name is Tiffany Darwish, launched her career with the now-legendary Shopping Mall Tour '87, performing free concerts at malls across the country beginning in June 1987. The grassroots campaign helped turn the then-15-year-old into a teen sensation before she became a chart-topping artist.

In September 1987, Tiffany's cover of Tommy James and the Shondells' 1967 hit "I Think We're Alone Now" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 less than two months after its release and made her a household name.

"I Think We're Alone Now" was the second single released from her self-titled debut album. She followed up with "Could've Been," the third single released from "Tiffany," which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. In addition, the album produced her Beatles cover "I Saw Him Standing There," which peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, and "Feelings of Forever," which reached the No. 50 spot.
Tiffany rose to fame at 15 with her hit song "I Think We're Alone Now." (Ron Eisenberg/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)

At 16, Tiffany became the youngest female artist to top the Billboard 200 with a debut album. She went on to headline her first major tour in 1988, with New Kids on the Block opening for her before the boy band's own meteoric rise.

However, Tiffany's chart dominance proved difficult to sustain. While her 1988 sophomore album, "Hold an Old Friend's Hand," was certified platinum by the RIAA and produced the Top 10 hit "All This Time," it fell short of matching the success of her debut. As the teen-pop landscape shifted in the early 1990s, her third album, "New Inside," failed to gain commercial traction.
RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

In 1993, Tiffany released her fourth album, "Dreams Never Die," which was issued only in Asian markets. Afterward, Tiffany largely stepped back from the mainstream music scene to focus on raising her son Elijah, whom she shares with her ex-husband, makeup artist Bulmaro Garcia. The two were married from 1992 to 2003.
In the early 2000s, Tiffany left Hollywood behind and moved to Nashville. During a 2023 interview with Fox News Digital, she explained why she decided to embrace a simpler life in Tennessee.
She became the youngest female artist to have an album top the Billboard 200. (Paul Massey/Mirrorpix/Getty Images)
DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME

"I came to Nashville for the first time when I was 10," the California native recalled. "I’ve been coming back ever since. I love being out in the country – I’m a country girl at heart. I’ve toured all over the world and this place has always been home for me. There’s just something about coming home to my little ranch… I’ve never looked back."

Since the days of her teenage stardom, Tiffany has continued to tour and release music as an independent artist. She has also made appearances in movies and television shows and starred in several reality TV series.

During a June interview with Fox News Digital, Tiffany detailed how she spent the past several years building a culinary brand that combines her love of cooking, entertaining and connecting with fans. Through her platform, "Let's Food With Tiffany," she offers recipes, virtual cooking experiences and food-focused events that showcase the same energy and creativity that made her a pop sensation.

Earlier this year, Tiffany released her second cookbook, "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ‘80s Kitchen Encore," which she created with Las Vegas celebrity chef Alicia Shevetone. "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ’80s Kitchen Encore" followed her first cookbook, "Breakfast with Tiffany," which she released independently.
Tiffany left Hollywood for Nashville in the early 2000s. (Lorne Thomson /Darlene Hammond)

In July, Tiffany announced that she would make her New York theatrical debut in "Spandex the Musical," in which she plays Linda Gustafson, a housewife who competes in the fictional 1988 Crystal Light National Aerobics Championship.
"I’ve always believed the right role would find me, and the moment I read the script, I knew Linda was that character," she told People magazine at the time.

"Just as Linda discovers a new passion through aerobics that changes her life, I’ve found exciting new passions beyond music through my ‘Pop Life’ cookbook, ‘Let’s Food With Tiffany’ events, and now returning to acting on stage," she continued. "It’s a reminder that it’s never too late to reinvent yourself."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"Spandex: The Musical" is a 10-day limited Off-Broadway engagement which runs through Sept. 27. After each performance, Tiffany performs "I Think We're Alone Now" during the curtain call.
She is currently starring in Off-Broadway's "Spandex: The Musical." (Bruce Glikas/Getty Images)

"There are so many wonderful parallels between Linda’s journey and my own, and I’m thrilled the producers have even woven in some fun Tiffany Easter eggs that I know longtime fans are going to love," she told People.

Tiffany said the project is especially meaningful because a portion of the show's proceeds will benefit Children's Miracle Network, a nonprofit organization that raises money for 170 children's hospitals across the United States and Canada.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Tiffany said that the role is a "dream come true." (Bruce Glikas/Getty Images)

"Making my Off-Broadway debut with such a funny, heartfelt and uplifting show is truly a dream come true," Tiffany said. "I’m also incredibly proud that ‘Spandex The Musical’ is partnering with Children’s Miracle Network, with a portion of the proceeds helping children and families in need."

"Giving back has always been close to my heart, so being able to combine my love of performing with a cause that means so much to me makes this experience even more special," she added.

"I can’t wait for audiences to experience the laughs, the music, the ‘80s nostalgia and, of course, plenty of spandex!"

title: Meghan Markle’s outing with Ellen DeGeneres exposes 'irony' in royal’s ‘quiet country life’: expert
summary: Meghan Markle's first photographed outing in the Cotswolds with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi raises questions about her quiet life claims.
story: Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," argues Prince Harry and Meghan Markle choose publicity while seeking privacy and says their royal status should be made clear.
Meghan Markle is raising questions after being photographed in England with two Hollywood stars.

The 45-year-old royal was recently photographed in the Cotswolds with Ellen DeGeneres and her wife, Portia de Rossi, in her first photographed outing since arriving in the U.K., which Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" said hints that "there is already going to be considerably less privacy for Meghan in Britain than perhaps she anticipated."

"But there is an irony here too. If Harry and Meghan genuinely wanted to disappear into quiet country life, the Cotswolds is one of the places where they could probably accomplish that," Schofield told Fox News Digital. "Instead, Meghan’s first photographed social outing is with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi. That tells me she remains very interested in celebrity and in being associated with recognizable, high-profile people."

Schofield added that she finds it "interesting" that Markle "appears to have changed countries without necessarily changing the social ecosystem she prefers," noting that when living in Montecito, she and Prince Harry were spending time with "wealthy, famous and influential people."
Markle was photographed with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi in her first public outing since moving back to England. (Harold Cunningham/Getty Images)
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE ACCUSED OF SEEKING ‘BEST OF BOTH WORLDS’ WITH UK MOVE: EXPERT

The idea that her first photographed outing since moving to the U.K. was with "two fellow American celebrity transplants" isn't "inherently wrong" in Schofield's eyes, but she argues that it challenges the "idea that Meghan has returned to Britain simply to embrace a quieter, more anonymous country life."
"If anything, this suggests she may be trying to recreate elements of Montecito in the Cotswolds: privacy when she wants it, but with a glamorous and recognizable social circle around her," she said.

Schofield also noted that Markle's behavior, in comparison to Prince Harry's, also highlights her interest "in commercial and monetary opportunities," while showing he is "determined to maintain the appearance and rhythm of royal life."

"Harry likes the engagements, the causes, the speeches and the sense of public duty," she said. "Meghan seems happier pursuing celebrity and commercial opportunities. title: Ed Sheeran concertgoers warn artists about sharing political views: 'You're going to alienate' fans
summary: Ed Sheeran fans at his Philadelphia concert warned artists that political statements alienate audiences. Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, planned for the weekend, were canceled due to weather.
story: The "Shape of You" singer held a solo concert last weekend in Philadelphia after Macklemore was dropped from the tour over his pro-Palestinian comments.

Several fans who attended Ed Sheeran’s concert in Philadelphia last weekend after Macklemore was dropped for making "Free Palestine" comments, warned other artists that if they make political statements, they will alienate half of their audience.

The "Bad Habits" singer was expected to play his second and third concerts since the controversy this Friday and Saturday at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, which is owned by Robert Kraft.
However, both shows have since been canceled.

"Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," tour promoter Messina Touring said in a statement on Friday. "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority."
ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT
Ed Sheeran is seen performing at a concert in December. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for iHeartRadio)
Previously, the New England Patriots owner allegedly threatened to cancel the concerts at his venue if Macklemore wasn’t taken off the tour, according to the "Thrift Shop" rapper.
Macklemore also claimed Kraft got other stadium owners to agree to not allow Sheeran to play at their venues if the rapper was still with his tour.

"The fact that they’re forcing Ed Sheeran to have an opinion is not right," one woman told Fox News Digital outside last Saturday’s concert. "He wants to stay in the middle – if you have an opinion, that’s fine, but you’re going to alienate at least 50% of your population, and it causes unrest."

title: Roseanne Barr calls former co-star a 'brainwashed bigot' after he said reboot was 'rightfully canceled'
summary: Roseanne Barr called Michael Fishman a "brainwashed bigot" on a podcast after he said the 2018 "Roseanne" hit reboot was "rightfully canceled."
story: Roseanne Barr told Fox News Digital she believes her upbringing was the perfect depiction of the American experience.
Roseanne Barr is firing back at her former co-star, calling him a "brainwashed bigot."

During a recent appearance on the "Can't Be Censored" podcast, the 73-year-old actress and comedian hit back at her former "Roseanne" co-star, Michael Fishman, after he said the 2018 reboot was "rightfully canceled."

"He f---ing doesn’t even f---ing know what I said, even though I’ve explained it 10,000 times for nine years on the internet," Barr said. "He hasn’t even taken the time to listen to what I say because he’s a bigot. And he’s a brainwashed bigot."

The reboot of the hit '90s show was a huge success when it premiered in March 2018 but was canceled just two months later after Barr tweeted a racist remark about Valerie Jarrett, a former advisor to former President Obama.
Barr fired back at her former co-star who said ABC was right to cancel the "Roseanne" reboot. (Getty Images)
ROSEANNE BARR REVEALS ‘DAMAGED’ HEART, FEARS SHE WILL ‘DIE ON THE SURGERY TABLE’

Barr apologized for the remark multiple times. However, ABC decided to fire her and cancel the show. A month later, the network announced a new spin-off called "The Connors," bringing back a majority of the "Roseanne" cast without any involvement from Barr.
The comedian went on to say that Fishman asked her about her comments "9,000" times before she told him to "go and f--- yourself and stay f---ed ‘till the day you die."

"Don’t put my name in your f---ng mouth; shut the f--- up," she recalled telling him. "You are an ignoramus and a bigot, and you have no idea what I said because it contradicts the Democratic Party platform that you’ve had shoved down your throat and up your a--. So, just f--- you. You have no geopolitical context whatsoever to discuss what I said."
Fishman fired back after Barr reignited their years-old feud, but the former child star appeared to take a different approach to the comedian’s blistering comments.

"I know everybody wants a response to Roseanne’s comments," Fishman said in a statement shared on social media, before taking a moment to thank Barr for acknowledging that he did reach out to her after her 2018 controversy.
Michael Fishman and Roseanne Barr appear in a 1990 episode of "Roseanne." (ABC Photo Archives / Getty Images)

Fishman continued to explain that he showed Barr "compassion" during her scandal, even though he "vehemently disagreed" with her. He said that her memory of how she responded to his attempts to discuss the issue was accurate, and that he'd kept the things she said to him to himself "for her protection."

"But I guess she gave you a glimpse into the darker side of my childhood," he admitted, before adding that he does have "tremendous gratitude" for the time he spent working with her on the original show.

The actor, who played D.J. Conner on "Roseanne," also reflected on the complicated nature of their relationship, saying, "I’m living something publicly that a lot of you have been navigating privately," referring to the experience of "caring and loving someone who’s been a powerful part of your life and who’s changed and we don’t understand. And we don’t agree with it."

He concluded his statement by saying, "I’m going to make art from the joy and the pain."
Metcalf said she hasn't spoken to Barr since they finished filming the reboot. (Adam Rose/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
In a recent interview with The New Yorker, Laurie Metcalf, who played Barr's sister, Jackie Harris, on the show, said the two "haven’t spoken since we said goodbye at the end of the reboot."
Barr confirmed she has not kept in touch with any of her former co-stars during an interview with Fox News Digital in June 2025.

"No, I'm not friends with none of them. They're all in the past," she said. "I have pleasant memories of what fun we had, wish them all the best. And, no, we don't talk. I've moved on from that horrendous ending and chapter of my life, but you know, I don't hold any bitterness or nothing to them. But, my God, what fun we had on that show.

title: Dolly Parton’s sisters push back on feud rumors after nephew’s legal battle with star's estate erupts

Dolly Parton’s sisters are shutting down claims of a family feud as tensions surrounding the late country legend’s legacy have spilled into court.

Nearly one month after Parton’s death, her sisters pushed back against reports of infighting within the family, insisting they remain united as a separate legal dispute involving the singer’s longtime manager and nephew resulted in a temporary restraining order.

"I’ll say this and this only: there is no feud within our family," Freida Parton shared Wednesday on Instagram. "No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate. We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other. I love you all!!"
DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH

Parton's sister Stella echoed Freida's message, emphasizing that the family remains united as it continues to navigate its grief.
"It has been a comfort to experience such an outpouring of love on [Dolly's] behalf as we grieve her passing," Stella posted Thursday on Instagram.
"We are also grieving the loss of our brother Denver who passed less than a month before her. All families have the same struggles since we are all living in this world having a human experience!
"We are still intact and moving forward because our children and grandchildren look to us for strength and guidance during this difficult time of loss and confusion for them as well," she added.

"Regardless of what you may have seen on different news outlets, we are all doing what you would be doing under the same circumstances, we are living our lives one day at a time and being grateful for every blessing."

Macklemore is taking his views on "Free Palestine" on the road.

The rapper, who was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour earlier this month after stirring controversy with his politically charged performances, announced Thursday that he's going on a new tour he's calling the "Free Palestine Tour."

"If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it’s that something has shifted over the last three years. Macklemore wrote that "what happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," and that "when the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

title: David Charvet admits he walked away from Hollywood after 'Baywatch' to focus on fatherhood
summary: David Charvet reveals why he left Hollywood over a decade ago and how "Special Forces: World's Toughest Test" let him prove something to his kids.
story: The former "Baywatch" star called his children his "legacy" and said he participated in "Special Forces" to show his children what he gave up for them.
David Charvet is opening up about why he left Hollywood.
In a new interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old actor discussed his experience on Fox's hit series, "Special Forces: World's Toughest Test," and why he stepped away from Hollywood in 2013.

"I left Hollywood because I wanted to be a good dad, and for me, today my children are my legacy," he said. "It's not the career you built or the money you have or all that. It's really what you leave behind. And what I'm leaving one day behind is really my children. And if I did it right in that way, then I think I've successfully done my job as a man on this planet. So, for me, there's no regrets."
Having left Hollywood over a decade ago, Charvet expressed how "honored" he is "to be amongst all these people and just to be a part of it."
Charvet quit acting in order to be a good father to his two kids, who he shares with his ex-wife, Brooke Burke. (Kim Raff/Getty Images for Operation Smile)
‘SPECIAL FORCES’ STARS JESSIE JAMES DECKER, HUSBAND ERIC SHARE KEY TO SUCCESSFUL 12-YEAR MARRIAGE
The actor became famous playing lifeguard Matt Brody on "Baywatch," saying no one told him that he "was going to be a 'Baywatch' guy forever," but he doesn't mind.

"That's where I got my start. The show was incredible, it reached everywhere around the world," he said. "I've had a lot of incredible opportunities from it. Incredible life lessons, incredible friendships and relationships, so for me, I'm just grateful, you know, I'm super happy with whatever the outcome has been."
WATCH: David Charvet admits he left Hollywood in order to be a good dad to his two kids
The original "Baywatch" helped launch not only Charvet's career, but also put Pamela Anderson, Carmen Electra and many of its other stars on the map.

It was announced in September 2025 that a reboot of the series starring a whole new batch of lifeguards was in the works. In addition to seasoned actors, including Stephen Amel and Shay Mitchell, the show is also a launching pad for acting newcomers, Brooks Nader, Livvy Dunne and Noah Beck.
Charvet starred as Matt Brody in "Baywatch." (Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"I got to say that what we created 25 years ago was very special. At the same time, there was only 14 channels at the time. So people got a chance to see that show more probably today than what people are going to see in the next season that's about to come," he said about the new series. "Our executive producers, which are, I believe, executive producers today, were real lifeguards, live the life as lifeguards, so there were real stories."

'BAYWATCH' STAR BROOKS NADER'S CONSERVATIVE PARENTS BANNED BIKINIS GROWING UP AS SHE SLIPS INTO RED SWIMSUIT

Charvet is excited to see what the new generation brings to the show, but admits, "getting people to really watch something today is more of a challenge," and says the writers have to be "more creative" now than before, adding, "They got their work cut out for them."
While he was considered a big star in his heyday, Charvet has "been out of the game" for over 20 years, and admits his "kids have never seen me on television or in movies or anything live."

He explained to Fox News Digital that that was part of the reason he agreed to compete on the show, noting it "was really important for me to maybe show them that aspect of what I kind of gave up for them." He shares two children with his ex-wife, Brooke Burke; a daughter, Rain and a son, Shaya.

"It's not every day that you get thrown out of a helicopter, or you jump out of 25 stories and things like that, and then also the mind games. Do I really have what it takes? To take on what we took on was a real thing that I wanted to see if I could do. So for me, it was a huge challenge, an incredible opportunity, and hopefully my kids will be proud."

title: ‘Rocky IV’ star Dolph Lundgren says he planned his own funeral during brutal cancer battle
summary: Dolph Lundgren reveals in his new memoir "Fights Worth Fighting" that he planned his own funeral during his nearly decade-long cancer battle.
story: Actor Dolph Lundgren joins Fox & Friends to discuss his new memoir ‘Fights Worth Fighting,’ his journey to Hollywood and his battle with cancer.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
Dolph Lundgren was preparing to die.

The Swedish actor, who famously played Soviet boxer Ivan Drago in "Rocky IV," has written a new memoir, "Fights Worth Fighting: Finding Strength in Struggle." In it, the 68-year-old details his grueling journey with cancer.
‘ROCKY’ STAR DOLPH LUNDGREN SWEARS BY THIS SECRET FOR STRONG MARRIAGE
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"Fights Worth Fighting: Finding Strength in Struggle" by Dolph Lundgren is available now. (Harper Horizon)
The star was diagnosed in 2015 after doctors found a cancerous tumor in his kidney. Lundgren had surgery to remove the tumor and continued appearing in movies like "Creed II" and "Aquaman."
After remaining cancer-free for five years, doctors discovered more tumors in 2020. He later learned the cancer had spread to his liver, both lungs, spine and in and around his left kidney.
Dolph Lundgren opened up about the dark moments in his cancer journey. (© Per Bernal)

"I had a lot of difficult conversations with myself," Lundgren told Fox News Digital. "I definitely had a few tough ones. Of course, as most older men do, you do estate planning. You plan your will and who's going to get what. But in this case, it was around the corner. It was something I had to plan a little more in detail, like funerals and trying to figure out where I would be, what would be better for my family. Planning your own funeral is kind of a saying, but I literally was doing that. That was tough."
WATCH: DOLPH LUNDGREN OPENS UP ABOUT CANCER BATTLE, BECOMING US CITIZEN IN ‘FIGHTS WORTH FIGHTING’
During that time, Lundgren said he considered ending his life.

"At some point, which was even harder, I started thinking, 'Do I really want to be in bed weighing 60 pounds and having people come and see me like that? Or should I just end it myself?'" Lundgren said. "I started considering that. I spoke to my brother. We made a deal, and he would help me out if it came to that, if I made that decision. But it was a tough conversation."
Swedish actor Dolph Lundgren with American actor, director and screenwriter Sylvester Stallone on the set of his movie "Rocky IV." (Sunset Boulevard/Corbis via Getty Images)

In the book, Lundgren wrote, "When I was deep into the cancer treatments and thinking about the possibility of killing myself, my brother, Johan, was going to help me, because I didn’t know what kind of condition I might be in once I made that decision. I could be in really bad shape by then and not capable of completing the suicide on my own."
Dolph Lundgren was diagnosed with kidney cancer in 2015. (Emma Krokdal)

"There are countries in Europe, like Switzerland, that permit legal suicide for people who are terminally ill, but I still might have needed someone there to help me," he continued. "Johan and I talked about it, but once I met Dr. Drakaki and began feeling a little better, it never went any further than that."
Lundgren’s longtime friend Johan Pramell also said in the memoir that the star "wanted to go out in glory like a Viking because he didn't want people to have to watch him suffer or fade away."
Dolph with his first wife, Anette, and daughters, Ida and Greta, on a family vacation. (Author's private collection)

Medical aid in dying is not synonymous with euthanasia, according to the Online Journal of Issues in Nursing. The journal states that laws allowing medical aid in dying permit eligible adults with terminal illnesses to self-administer medication when certain criteria are met.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Dolph Lundgren and his cat, Bello, on his birthday. (Emma Krokdal)
Euthanasia, which is not legal in the United States, occurs when someone other than the patient administers medication with the intent of hastening the patient’s death, the journal states.
According to Dignity in Dying, a U.K.-based advocacy organization, 10 countries in Europe have laws that allow people experiencing "unbearable suffering" to access assisted dying.
Dolph Lundgren told Fox News Digital he wrote his memoir in hopes it will inspire others to keep fighting. (Emma Krokdal)
But one thing was certain — Lundgren wasn't ready to die.
Dolph Lundgren is seen here throwing a punch during treatment. (Emma Krokdal)

"I have a certain discipline, a fighter's heart, since I was a kid," he told Fox News Digital. "I think that was helpful. I may have had these thoughts, but the other side of me wants to go another round to see what happens. Maybe the other guy will drop. You never know. I think that's a part of it."

"But also, I believe being in good physical shape helped me, and continuing to work out through the whole thing," he said. "As much as I could, I would stay physically active. And then I was lucky to have my wife, who was very supportive, and my daughters."
A second opinion changed everything for Dolph Lundgren in his quest to be cancer-free. (Daniele Venturelli/Daniele Venturelli/Getty Images)
"They're the ones that kept me going by just their sheer presence," he added.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Dolph Lundgren and his wife are seen here in Greece. (Author's private collection)

At one point, a doctor in the U.K. told Lundgren he likely had two or three years left to live. Lundgren wrote in his memoir that he believed, based on the doctor's tone, his prognosis could have been closer to one or two years.

After returning to Los Angeles, Lundgren sought a second opinion from Dr. Alexandra Drakaki, an oncologist at UCLA Health, whom he credited with saving his life. "At this point, I was depressed and had almost given up all hope," he wrote.
Dolph Lundgren poses for photographers at the Jameson Empire Film Awards held at the Grosvenor House Hotel, Park Lane, in London on March 25, 2012. (Carl Cour/AFP via Getty Images)
According to the memoir, Drakaki determined that his cancer had been misdiagnosed, leading to a different treatment approach.
"What she found was that my 'kidney cancer' cells had a mutation that is fairly common in lung cancer," he wrote. "That's why the medications I had been given for the past two years weren't working."
Dolph Lundgren is seen here becoming a U.S. citizen in 2024. (Emma Krokdal)
After Lundgren went public with his cancer battle, one heavyweight stood in his corner: Sylvester Stallone.

"Stallone and I have a long history, a good, long relationship together," he said. "We've known each other for 40 years. We've made six films together over that period. He went from being a mentor, a boss on set, director, producer. I was just a new kid on the block. And then slowly, we moved together and became more equals, I would say, two older guys who've been in the business a long time. And he has three daughters, I have two, and we share that as well."
Dolph Lundgren is seen here training at a martial arts camp. (Author's private collection)

"When I got sick, he reached out to me," Lundgren said. "It was unexpected because he was the first one, actually, who reached out of everybody, even before some of my family, when it came out. And he was very emotional about it. It touched me. And that was another side of him that I'd never seen. Since then, we've been very close friends, even closer than before."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Dolph Lundgren (right) is seen with Sylvester Stallone (left) and Jenny Sandersson on the set of a Tecate beer commercial. (Author's private collection)
In November 2024, Lundgren announced he was cancer-free. In his memoir, he reflects on whether performance-enhancing drugs may have played a role in his cancer battle.

Lundgren wrote that he used anabolic steroids and other performance-enhancing drugs on and off from 1986 to 1996 while preparing for physically demanding movie roles. While he stressed that there is "no conclusive evidence" the drugs caused his cancer, he acknowledged they "might have helped cause" it, adding that he could not say for certain.
Dolph Lundgren with daughters Ida Lundgren, left, and Greta Lundgren attending the "Aquaman" premiere held at Cineworld in Leicester Square, London. (Ian West/PA Images via Getty Images)

"I wanted to be candid about my past and what I've been through," Lundgren explained. "And I think nobody knows what steroids and other performance-enhancing drugs do to us. The data is not conclusive. And I always thought it could not help me in my medical situation. I wanted to express a caution to people, to other young men, who may decide to try it, that it's not without risk."
Dolph Lundgren is seen in New York City on Sept. 22, 2026. (GC Images)

"I try to forgive and let go of everything from my past," he said. "That's very important to me. So, I don't blame myself. I was younger. I wasn't as smart as I am now. And I had pressures from the business. Is it really good for you? I doubt it. I really do."
Now, Lundgren said he still has plenty of fight in him.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Dolph Lundgren attends a photocall on June 22, 2024, in Santa Margherita di Pula, Italy. (Daniele Venturelli/Daniele Venturelli/Getty Images)

"I've obviously touched a lot of people as an actor in my business, and that's good," he said. "I've brightened up people's lives. I think that's great. That makes me feel good. I now hope to offer a little inspiration to others. I know I have so much more I want to do."

title: George Clooney rushes to Rande Gerber and Cindy Crawford's side after son Presley's death
summary: George Clooney arrived at Kaia Gerber's Los Angeles home to support Rande Gerber and Cindy Crawford after Presley Gerber's "suspected overdose."
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses the Presley Gerber death investigation, college drug fatalities and his book 'The Angels Among Us' on 'America's Newsroom.'
George Clooney rushed to Rande Gerber and Cindy Crawford's side days after their only son, Presley Gerber, died of a "suspected overdose."
The "Ocean's Eleven" actor and wife Amal Clooney were spotted arriving Tuesday at Kaia Gerber's home in Los Angeles, Calif.
Clooney, 65, a longtime friend of the family, who also launched multiple businesses with Rande, was reportedly referred to as "Uncle George" by the Gerber kids.
PRESLEY GERBER'S FINAL HOURS AT REHAB IN FOCUS AMID CAUSE OF DEATH QUESTIONS
George Clooney and wife Amal Clooney arrived at Kaia Gerber's house days after the death of Presley Gerber. (Getty Images/The Image Direct)
"George would spend hours talking to Presley," a source told the Daily Mail. "George is the nicest guy in the world and would do anything to help Rande's family."

"Especially after Presley got a DUI (in 2018), George would advise, 'Don't do that, it's not smart. Be careful.' More recently, George shared loving notes like, 'I am here for you,' that kind of stuff."
PRESLEY GERBER DEAD AT 27: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT CINDY CRAWFORD, RANDE GERBER'S FAMILY
The source noted that Clooney was "close" with Presley, who he considered "more than just a friend's kid; they had a bond."
The "Good Night, and Good Luck" actor will now reportedly focus on how he can best support his friend's family.
"He feels absolutely awful for Rande and the entire family, and he wants them to know that he is there for them in any way, shape or form," the insider said.
George Clooney and wife Amal Clooney exited a black SUV at Kaia Gerber's home. (The Image Direct)
"George has always been the person people turn to when they're going through something, and with something of this magnitude, that isn't going to change."
KID ROCK CALLS PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH A ‘TRAGEDY’ AS EX-GIRLFRIEND SAYS HE ‘DESERVED MORE TIME’

They added, "It doesn't matter how busy he is or what he has going on in his own life — if Rande or anyone in the family needs him, everything else stops. It's really that simple. That's what family does."
Rande became a prominent figure in the hospitality industry years ago through his Gerber Group, which operated bars, lounges and restaurants in hotels and entertainment venues around the world.

George Clooney, Amal Clooney, Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber attend the Clooney Foundation for Justice Inaugural Albie Awards at New York Public Library on Sept. 29, 2022. (Getty Images for Albie Awards)
Rande later joined forces with Clooney and real estate developer Mike Meldman to create Casamigos tequila. The brand began as a private venture among friends before becoming a major spirits company.

Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber take a walk Anthe beach in Mexico with their children Kaia Gerber and, Presley Gerber on January 3, 2011. (Denise Truscello/WireImage)

Gerber said he and "The Boys" arrived at Clooney’s home to find black designer luggage bags at each place setting on the table. When they opened the bags, they found "a million dollars in 20 dollar bills," E! News reported.

"George begins to say, ‘Listen, I want you guys to know how much you’ve meant to me and how much you mean to me in my life,’" Rande recalled. "'I came to L.A., I slept on your couch. I’m so fortunate in my life to have all of you and I couldn’t be where I am today without all of you. So, it was really important to me that while we’re still all here together, that I give back. Gerber added, "Every one of us – 14 of us – got a million dollars. Every single one of us. We’re in shock."

Rande Gerber and George Clooney founded Casamigos Tequila with Mike Meldman in 2013. (David Bennet)
Gerber said some of their friends were going through a difficult time, including one who was working at a Texas airport's bar trying to make ends meet for his family.

PRESLEY GERBER, SON OF CINDY CRAWFORD AND RANDE GERBER, DEAD AT 27
Gerber took the money and donated it to charity. "This is who George is. That was September 27th, 2013. Now September 27th, 2014, he marries Amal. Now that’s good karma right there," Gerber said.

Shortly after the Clooneys welcomed their twins in 2017, George and Rande sold their Casamigos tequila brand for $1 billion to British beverage giant Diageo. The pair, along with partner Mike Meldman, created the brand in 2013.

title: 'Home Improvement' star Jonathan Taylor Thomas arrested for alleged public intoxication, resisting deputy
summary: Former "Home Improvement" child star Jonathan Taylor Thomas was detained in Westlake Village, California, after reportedly exiting a vehicle.
story: ‘Home Improvement’ actor Richard Karn tells Fox News Digital his dad’s reaction to co-star and Playboy model Pamela Anderson joining the show.
"Home Improvement" star Jonathan Taylor Thomas was detained after reportedly resisting an officer in Westlake Village, California, Monday.
According to court records obtained by Fox News Digital, Thomas was detained at the Malibu/Lost Hills sheriff's station. After being booked, Thomas was released.

Law enforcement sources told TMZ the child actor was a passenger in a vehicle that was stopped by police. The outlet reported that deputies told Thomas to stay inside the vehicle, but he allegedly exited anyway. Thomas was also reportedly drunk at the time of the incident.
Jonathan Taylor Thomas, a child star in "Home Improvement," was reportedly detained for resisting an officer in California Monday. (Getty Images)
‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’ STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS MAKES RARE APPEARANCE IN REUNION PHOTO WITH CO-STARS

"He was uncooperative with them, failed to follow orders, and obstructed the investigation, so he was arrested for obstruction, and he was arrested for drunk in public."

title: Dolly Parton’s legacy battle escalates as manager granted restraining order against star's nephew
summary: Danny Nozell's restraining order request against Bryan Seaver revealed alleged threats to destroy Dolly Parton's brand partnerships after her death.
story: Fox News contributor Billy Bush breaks down the court battle emerging between the singer’s nephew and her manager on ‘The Story.’
A bitter battle over Dolly Parton’s legacy took a dramatic turn when her longtime manager sought a restraining order against the country icon’s nephew.

Danny Nozell, who runs She's Alive, LLC, an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests, filed for a restraining order against Bryan Seaver in Nashville, according to The Associated Press.

A Tennessee judge granted the temporary restraining order Wednesday, citing a pattern of alleged threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver’s "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order called the communications "concerning" and specifically pointed to an alleged threat to use force.

The order barred Seaver and his company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, which provided Parton’s security detail, from entering She’s Alive properties or coming within 1,000 feet of its employees and business partners. It also prohibited Seaver from contacting them.
DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY
Dolly Parton’s longtime manager, Danny Nozell, filed for a restraining order against Dolly Parton’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, after alleged threatening messages. (Katherine Bomboy/NBC via Getty Images)
Parton chose Seaver to publicly announce her death. The singer-songwriter died Aug. 25. Less than a month later, a behind-the-scenes feud erupted into a legal battle.

Nozell and She's Alive accused Seaver of sending increasingly threatening messages in the weeks leading up to their request for a temporary restraining order. The filing came after She’s Alive fired Seaver over his alleged "terrorizing conduct."
Court documents obtained by The Associated Press show text messages and emails allegedly sent by Seaver.
The messages initially included threats to destroy the brand and, after Parton’s death, allegedly showed Seaver reveling in his newfound fame and calling himself an "international arms dealer."

Danny Nozell and She’s Alive, LLC, accused Bryan Seaver of "terrorizing conduct" before firing Bryan Seaver from the company. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

In one message written Sept. 1 and included in the court documents, Seaver said, "I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f---ing pay me."

According to the court documents, the alleged messages rattled those within Parton’s business circle, leading several employees to resign and her trust and estate attorney to step away. She’s Alive also brought in private security to protect employees at work and at their homes.
She's Alive terminated Seaver Sept. 15 and asked the court to bar Parton's nephew from contacting or coming within 1,000 feet of its employees, attorneys and business partners.

The alleged messages reportedly prompted employees to resign, an attorney to leave and She’s Alive to hire private security. (Courtesy of Dolly Parton's Imagination Library)

"I am a career soldier and military contractor and do conduct arms deals for foreign governments. I am a security professional, and I am a killer," he told the outlet. "However, nothing in this lawsuit were threats, and most of the comments I stand by."
He claimed the messages had been taken out of context to make them appear threatening.

"I was talking frankly in a private way with Danny, who I thought was my friend, and he fancies himself a gangster," he said. "A lot of these messages are two guys having rage talk and crying on the phone together while we were grieving."

title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for 2006 sex crime in New York
summary: Harvey Weinstein apologized while maintaining his innocence, and a Manhattan judge called him a sexual predator and the face of the #MeToo movement.
story: Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison after being convicted in a New York retrial of sexually assaulting former TV production assistant Miriam Haley at his Manhattan apartment in 2006.
Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced movie mogul, was sentenced in Manhattan to 15 years in prison Wednesday for a felony sex crime in another #MeToo reckoning.

Weinstein’s sentencing for sexually assaulting one-time TV production assistant Miriam Haley followed a legal odyssey spanning more than six years. His 2020 conviction was overturned by New York's highest court. A second jury found Weinstein guilty again at a retrial last year.

Once among the most powerful figures in the entertainment industry, Weinstein was an Oscar-winning producer whose hits included "Shakespeare in Love," "Pulp Fiction" and "Chocolat." But his downfall came quickly after sexual assault allegations in 2017 set off the #MeToo movement.

Weinstein, 74, is expected to appeal and maintains that he never raped or sexually assaulted anyone. He is now likely to remain behind bars well into his 80s. Seated in a wheelchair, he was quickly moved out of the courtroom after the sentencing, while some of his accusers hugged and brushed away tears.
JONATHAN TURLEY: WHEN JOURNALISTS WHINE ABOUT #METOO, THEY DON’T MEAN PLATNER, TOO
Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison in Manhattan after his conviction for sexually assaulting Miriam Haley. (Dean Moses/amNewYork via AP, Pool)
Weinstein and his victim both spoke in court

Weinstein faced up to 25 years in prison for sexually assaulting Haley at his Manhattan apartment in 2006. He has already served more than six years as his case cycled through the criminal justice system. Haley gave her account of the assault at two trials and again addressed the court Wednesday.

"Having been sexually assaulted by Harvey Weinstein has had a devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away. Making the decision to speak up will have me looking over my shoulder for years to come," Haley said.
"It’s a life sentence for me."
Minutes later, Weinstein apologized while reiterating his innocence.

"Reflecting on all that has happened since 2017 has helped me recognize how my past conduct has negatively affected others. I live with many regrets and sincerely apologize to anyone I have affected with my actions," he said.
EX-MAYOR FOUND LIABLE FOR ALLEGED SEXUAL ASSAULTS OF 7 WOMEN, ORDERED TO PAY $13M
Harvey Weinstein, 74, was sentenced Wednesday to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting former TV production assistant Miriam Haley. (AP Photo/Michael Sisak)
Some of his accusers who were in court shook their heads while he spoke.
Judge Curtis Farber said Weinstein was once a king in the movie industry, "but recognition for these achievements will pale in comparison to what you did."
He said Weinstein is now known as "a sexual predator, the literal face of the #MeToo movement."
The judge said Weinstein treated women as "mere objects to be played with and discarded" and still hasn’t accepted responsibility, portraying himself as a victim during jailhouse interviews.
Haley afterward said she was happy with the sentence, while saying it's clear that Weinstein has not acknowledged what he did.
"I think he still feels entitled, and that’s part of the problem," she said.
ARMIE HAMMER COMPARES HIS HOLLYWOOD EXILE TO BEING CRUCIFIED: 'THE NAILS ARE IN MY HANDS'
Harvey Weinstein received a 15-year prison sentence after a retrial again found him guilty of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley. (AP Photo/Michael Sisak)
Haley’s lawyer, the famed victims’ rights attorney Gloria Allred, rejected any suggestion that Weinstein’s sentencing means the #MeToo era is over.
"Women are empowered in a way they have never been before," she said.
Weinstein was originally sentenced to 23 years in prison after a jury convicted him of assaulting Haley and raping an aspiring actress, Jessica Mann, in 2013.

Tried for a second time last year, he was again convicted of a first-degree criminal sex act for assaulting Haley, who has also gone by the name Mimi Haleyi. In a messy split verdict, the jury acquitted him of forcibly performing oral sex on another woman, Kaja Sokola, and could not reach a verdict on a rape charge involving Mann.
After another retrial ended in a hung jury in May, Manhattan prosecutors dropped the rape charge rather than pursue a fourth trial after Mann said she could not bear to testify again.
Weinstein’s health issues pushed the defense to ask for leniency.
SETH ROGEN REFUSES TO OFFER JAMES FRANCO A SECOND CHANCE AFTER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT CLAIMS
Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison after a yearslong legal battle that included the reversal of his 2020 conviction. (Steven Hirsch/New York Post via AP, Pool)
Defense lawyer Jacob Kaplan wanted three more years on top of the six years Weinstein already served, saying a longer sentence would make it more likely that Weinstein dies in prison.
Weinstein has been in the hospital six times since 2025, Kaplan said, while dealing with blood cancer, congestive heart failure and kidney issues.

Weinstein is also awaiting resentencing in a separate rape case in Los Angeles. A California appeals court upheld the 2022 conviction but threw out his original 16-year sentence because the judge had considered his New York convictions — that were later thrown out — as an aggravating factor.

After shuffling between state prison, where he tested positive for COVID-19 early in the pandemic, and New York City’s notorious Rikers Island complex, Weinstein has been housed at a medical unit for inmates at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan.
Haley, 49, is a former entertainment producer now working in advertising.
She said she met Weinstein through a mutual connection and worked briefly as a production assistant on "Project Runway," a reality competition show that he produced.
FOUR MORE WOMEN ACCUSE FORMER NFL PLAYER OF SEXUAL ASSAULT AMID EXISTING ALLEGATIONS: 'BLATANT LIES'
Harvey Weinstein maintained his innocence and apologized to people affected by his past conduct before a judge sentenced him to 15 years in prison. (Steven Hirsch/New York Post via AP, Pool)

Haley said she accepted an invitation to visit Weinstein’s apartment, and, after chatting briefly, he lunged to kiss her, she testified. She said she rebuffed him, but he grabbed her, forcibly backed her into a bedroom and sexually assaulted her, ignoring her pleas to stop.
She recalled Weinstein asking, "Don’t you think we’re much closer now?" after either the alleged assault or a subsequent occasion when she says she had unwanted, but not forced, sex with him.
She also recalled telling him after the second encounter, "You know you can’t keep doing this."

title: Judge Judy says those who don't like America should 'go somewhere else'
summary: Judge Judy doubles down on her love of America, praising capitalism and personal responsibility. The TV icon also addresses 1950s nostalgia and a longing for law and order.
story: Fran Weinstein shares how Judge Judy responded to a matchmaking request with a bold take on independence. The retired "Entertainment Tonight" producer has written a memoir, "Tortured Soles."
Judge Judy is doubling down on her love of America, telling people who want to fundamentally change the country to "go somewhere else."
During an interview with USA Today, Judy Sheindlin, 83, opened up about her views on America and the enduring popularity of her courtroom television persona.
"I have a house, and I have a home. I consider America my home. America has been good to me. I think that it’s the greatest country in the world," Sheindlin said.
JUDGE JUDY PREPARING TO END DECADES-LONG RUN AS TV'S TOUGHEST JUDGE
Judge Judy tells America's critics to "go somewhere else." (Getty Images for Keep Memory Alive)

"If you don’t like this country, go somewhere else," she continued. "Don’t come to the greatest country in the world, the most successful country in the world, and say, ‘I want to change it.’ There are other countries that are the something else that you want. Go there. Go there. But don’t come into my home and say, ‘I want to change it.’"
"We are a capitalist country that revered excellence, that revered entrepreneurship, that revered all the things that made us great," she added. "Whether you like it or not, it's there."
Sheindlin’s comments came as CBS celebrated the 30th anniversary of "Judge Judy" with the primetime special "Judge Judy: Unfiltered, Unforgettable."

The TV icon also addressed the growing nostalgia for an earlier era, suggesting that many people are craving elements of the 1950s — including a greater sense of order, personal responsibility and common decency.

title: 'Lioness' star weighs in on what drove Taylor Sheridan's unexpected decision for her character
summary: Elizaveta Neretin reacts to Taylor Sheridan's outcome for her "Lioness" character Oleksandra Balakin in the season 3 finale.
story: Laysla De Oliveira and Jill Wagner told Fox News Digital how the third season of Taylor Sheridan's hit series will be different from the rest.
WARNING: Spoilers below.
"Lioness" star Elizaveta Neretin reacted to Taylor Sheridan's bombshell season 3 finale, which saw her character, Oleksandra Balakin, killed off.

Speaking to Fox News Digital, Neretin — who played the Ukrainian double agent — said she expected Oleksandra's fate. The character had been captured by American forces and recruited to help rescue Joe (Zoe Saldaña) after she was kidnapped.
Elizaveta Neretin plays Oleksandra Balakin in "Lioness." (Lauren "Lo" Smith/Paramount+)
In the episode, which aired Sunday night, Oleksandra was killed.
'LIONESS' SEASON 3 FINALE REVEALS WHO ORCHESTRATED JOE'S KIDNAPPING ALL ALONG

"I thought it was going to happen. So when he called, and he told me, I was like, 'Yeah, I get it.' I'm sad for Oleksandra and what Oleksandra represents, but I understand the choice. It does serve this. It serves to show how the whole system is. Like American or not American, the whole system and the people that work in the system. It's all sharks, you know, so it just demonstrates how people are," she told Fox News Digital.
Taylor Sheridan is the creator behind "Lioness." (Dominique Charriau/WireImage)
Neretin said she would have preferred a different outcome for Oleksandra but understood why Sheridan made the decision.
"I would love a different ending for her, but like I said, I understand why it had to happen."

"I would love a different ending for her, but like I said, I understand why it had to happen. But, of course, I would have a good ending for her. I just wonder if being a triple agent, I think your days are numbered. I don't think you can pull that off and live to an old age unless you give up on family you have, which I don't think she would."

"If you give up on the family you have, perhaps you could find a way to hide somewhere, you know what I mean? But the way she fights for her country, I think she cares way too much, way more about that outcome than her life. I think that she made that decision a long time ago," Neretin said.
Elizaveta Neretin as Oleksandra in "Lioness." (Credit: Paramount+)

The actress said she never asked Sheridan whether he had considered an alternative ending for Oleksandra. Instead, she trusted his creative judgment and did not try to challenge him while working on the series.

And he was like, 'Yeah, that works,'" she began. "I didn't challenge him, it was very interesting, like he runs the show, you know what I mean? He's the boss."
Nicole Kidman as Kaitlyn in "Lioness." (Ryan Green/Paramount+)
