title: Mistress may have handed prosecutors missing ‘why’ in ‘American Idol’ alum’s wife murder case: expert
summary: The Caleb Flynn trial took a dramatic turn as mistress Alleigha Botner read explosive texts exchanged in the months before Ashley Flynn's fatal shooting.
story: Fox News contributor Josh Ritter explains why the latest testimony could influence jurors, from motive and text messages to the missing murder weapon.

The explosive testimony of Caleb Flynn's former mistress may have handed Ohio prosecutors a critical piece of their murder case against the former "American Idol" contestant – a potential answer to why he would allegedly kill his wife, a former prosecutor told Fox News Digital.

"Motive. She provides a motive," Josh Ritter, a former prosecutor, criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor, said of Alleigha Botner's testimony. "She gives jurors a reason for why would this man murder his wife."
"She seems like she was, by all accounts, a very nice woman," Ritter said about Ashley Flynn. "She's the mother of his children. Yes, he wanted out of the marriage."
"Perhaps there was some financial gain in the idea of life insurance, but, you know, jurors oftentimes struggle with that question," he added.
DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)

Flynn is accused of fatally shooting his wife in the back of the head inside their Ohio home on Feb. 16 and staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in. He has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges.
Botner, who testified she carried on an affair with Flynn for roughly a year and a half, spent two days walking jurors through many of the 107,000-plus messages exchanged during their relationship.
NEW JERSEY MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE WITH BARBELL ALLEGEDLY CONFESSED IN MESSAGES TO RELATIVES: REPORT
Some contained explicit discussions about Ashley's death.
In one May 2025 message, Flynn allegedly wrote, "If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat."
RUSSIAN SPIES ORCHESTRATED $40K MURDER PLOT IN NATION’S CAPITAL, US ALLEGES
Days later, he allegedly wrote, "I hate her, loathe her. I want her dead."
In June, Flynn allegedly told Botner, "Please hire someone to take [her] out. I need you in my life, I need you."
Alleigha Botner wipes away tears while testifying about messages exchanged with Caleb Flynn during his murder trial in Ohio. (CREDIT: WKEF)
SCOTT PETERSON'S DEFENSE LOSES BID TO INTRODUCE WITNESS TESTIMONY IN LONG-RUNNING FIGHT TO OVERTURN CONVICTION
Botner responded, "So tempting. I can't live without you. And I've had this thought so often lately. How do we figure this out?"
Botner also became emotional while reading one of her own messages to Flynn, expressing regrets that she wished she never wrote it.
ALEX MURDAUGH LAWYERS ALLEGE ‘FABRICATED’ EVIDENCE WAS USED TO SECURE MURDER INDICTMENTS
"I want to kill her, Caleb," she had written.
"That makes two of us," Flynn allegedly responded.
Body camera footage shows Caleb Flynn reacting to his wife’s murder inside their home in Tipp City, Ohio on Feb. 16, 2026. (Tipp City Police Department)
ALEX MURDAUGH MAKES 'EXPLOSIVE' BID TO BLOW UP MURDER CASE HINGING ON DNA, DIRTY MONEY AND LIES: EXPERT
Ritter said it is the substance of those exchanges – rather than simply the existence of the affair or sheer volume of messages – that could prove significant for prosecutors.

"It's the idea that he's even discussing her being dead," Ritter said. "He went as far as to saying I literally would kill her. That's far beyond someone voicing their frustrations and venting to a lover that I wish my wife wasn't around, I wish she would leave, I wish we could get a divorce."
"This is saying you want that person dead, that, in your view, that is your solution to the problem that you have," he added.
Ashley Flynn, a Tipp City Schools substitute teacher and volleyball coach, was found dead in her Ohio home. (Tipp City Schools)
The messages grew particularly significant as prosecutors moved jurors closer to the night Ashley was killed.
FLORIDA PLASTIC SURGEON FOUND GUILTY OF MURDERING ATTORNEY WHO VANISHED FROM BLOODY OFFICE
Botner testified that Flynn told her in an August message he had stayed up until 4 a.m. "literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."

Months later, Botner gave Flynn a Jan. 11 ultimatum to leave Ashley or she would end their relationship. When he failed to do so, Botner cut off communication until Feb. 14 – just two days before Ashley's death.
By the night of Feb. 15, the two were communicating again.
Botner testified that Flynn discussed his plans for the following day, including telling family members about the divorce and obtaining a burner phone.
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)
Shortly after midnight, Flynn allegedly wrote to Botner, "It's happening."
He then wrote, "February 16th – day I'll never forget."
"You're about to be free," Botner responded.
"I choose you," Flynn replied.
Those were some of the final messages Flynn sent Botner before she learned Ashley had been killed, she testified.
Ritter pointed to that timing as among the most significant evidence Botner brought to the prosecution's case.
He noted that Flynn had spent months allegedly talking about wanting Ashley dead before the messages reached the eve of her killing.

"The day before the murder takes place, he tells his mistress that tomorrow is going to be a big day, that he chooses her," Ritter explained. "He's made a decision and that tomorrow, meaning February 16th, the date his wife was murdered, will be a day that he will never forget."

Alleigha Botner testifies Wednesday in the Ohio murder trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn. Prosecutors say Botner had an affair with Flynn before his wife, Ashley Flynn, was killed. (CREDIT: WKEF)
But Ritter said the same enormous volume of messages prosecutors are using against Flynn also gives his attorneys an argument.

The defense can contend prosecutors have cherry-picked the most damaging statements from more than 100,000 messages exchanged during an intense affair and stripped them of the broader context of two people using exaggerated and sometimes ugly language.
Flynn's attorneys can also argue that when he talked about what would happen Feb. 16, he was referring to finally leaving Ashley – not killing her.
WATCH: Caleb Flynn had ominous response when mistress said ‘I want to kill her’

"That could be true," Ritter said. "It could be that he is just the unluckiest man on earth, that the day he tells his mistress he's going to announce to his wife that he's leaving her after months of saying that he wants her dead, that some random home burglar happens to break in with no signs of forced entry, goes to his vehicle, knows exactly where to find his handgun, marches upstairs, puts two bullets in the back of his wife's head while she's sleeping, and leaves the rest of the house undisturbed."
During cross-examination Thursday, Flynn's attorneys began putting Botner's own language before the jury.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"I'm so done with you. You have murdered my heart," Botner acknowledged writing Flynn during one argument. "I hope you're glad you took my virginity and also my heart and stomped all over it. Enjoy your marriage. I'm done."

The defense also has another potentially important distinction to emphasize, Ritter said. Despite Flynn's repeated statements about wanting Ashley dead, he never explicitly told Botner he intended to carry out her killing.
"There was never an explicit mention of, 'I'm going to do it, I'm gonna follow through on it,'" Ritter said.
Caleb and Ashley Flynn are pictured in an undated photograph. (Ashley Flynn/Facebook)
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"I think they are also going to concentrate on the idea, as they have since opening statements, that this might have been a rush to judgment, that once police uncovered the affair, they stopped their investigation," Ritter said. "And once they knew that he was planning on leaving his wife, they thought, 'Well, that's enough for us. We're not going to pursue other leads.'"
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
"I'm not saying that's a convincing argument, but I'm saying that that is at least something for them to stand on and mount a defense on his behalf," he added.
WATCH: Caleb Flynn mistress drops bombshells in dramatic testimony
SEND US A TIP
The defense can also point to the absence of the alleged murder weapon, an eyewitness to the shooting and gunshot residue on Flynn.
GOT A TIP?
Botner testified, however, that Flynn had previously shown her a gun he kept inside the center console of his truck, though she could not remember what it looked like.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
"In an ideal world, would the prosecution want the murder weapon? Sure," Ritter said. "But ... it's something that the defense is obviously going to lean into."
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
But for Ritter, Botner's testimony ultimately comes back to the question prosecutors hope jurors will ask when they consider the killing – why?

"Motive," Ritter said. "She provides motive."

title: The frat omertà: Whistleblower warns of ‘code of silence’ after Ole Miss deaths, alleged Penn State coke ring
summary: The Ole Miss student death and Penn State cocaine ring allegations echo a deeper crisis in Greek life, says fraternity hazing survivor Andrew Lohse.
story: Former Dartmouth fraternity member Andrew Lohse breaks down why he believes a culture of silence enables dangerous hazing and drug rings. He urges incoming college students to carefully weigh the downside risks before pledging.
"You need a code of omertà if you're trying to create an organization that's essentially like a criminal organization," Andrew Lohse said.
Lohse was talking about fraternities – the 36-year-old is a fraternity hazing survivor and the author of "Confessions of an Ivy League Frat Boy."
As a Dartmouth student, the whistleblower exposed the stomach-turning indoctrination rituals he said he endured inside Sigma Alpha Epsilon.
TWO OLE MISS STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS PACKAGED KRATOM IS RECOVERED AT TWO SITES: OFFICIALS
Robert Strang, 20, an Ole Miss student, was found dead this week. (Strang Family)

When recent headlines came to light regarding the mysterious deaths of two students at Ole Miss – one of whom was in a fraternity – and the alleged frat cocaine distribution ring at Penn State, Lohse said he was immediately reminded of his time as a brother.
"For years and years [the last] 10 years, it's like whenever someone dies in a frat, like that's when my phone rings," Lohse told Fox News Digital.
OLE MISS NAMES STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS OFFICIAL ADDRESSES POTENTIAL FOR FOUL PLAY

One of the Ole Miss students who was found dead this past week, Ryan Strang, was a Phi Delta Theta fraternity brother. He was found at an off-campus home. Authorities found packages of kratom, a commercially available drug that has been derided as "gas station heroin," at both scenes. However, its role in either death was not immediately clear.
Phi Delta Theta has not been accused of any wrongdoing.

General view of Phi Delta Theta fraternity house on the campus of the University of Mississippi, Oxford, MS, September 24, 2026. Black ribbons are tied to the columns of the porch in honor of the death of fraternity member, 20-year-old Robert Strang from Atlanta. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)

"The loss of two young lives is a profound tragedy," the fraternity said in a statement, in part. "Phi Delta Theta joins the University of Mississippi and the broader Ole Miss community in mourning Robert and Aidan Hamilton and extending our deepest sympathies to their families, friends, chapter brothers, classmates, and all those who knew and loved them.

"These losses reinforce the importance of a collective commitment to health, safety, and well-being on college campuses today. We encourage the Phi Delta Theta community to keep the Strang family, the Mississippi Alpha Chapter, and everyone affected by these tragic losses in their thoughts."
Dangers like kratom did not exist when Lohse was in school, he said.
"There was no kratom, no tranq, no smoking bath salts, no fentanyl. Back then, the cocaine was more or less just cocaine. It wasn't like every time somebody did cocaine they could die."
OLE MISS TOXICOLOGY REPORTS EXPECTED SOON AND RESULTS MAY TRIGGER ANTI-FENTANYL LAW, OFFICIAL SAYS

At Penn State, prosecutors allege in court documents that pledges were allegedly coerced into cutting and packaging cocaine as part of an alleged organized drug ring led by former Sigma Chi member Agostino Abbatiello.
Agostino Abbateillo, 24, is one of 14 men charged with operating a massive cocaine ring near Penn State’s campus. (Getty Images: Grichka Beysson-Leandri; Kamil Krzaczynski for Fox News Digital)
Lohse said, "When I was reading that the pledges were in the background doing that, I thought that was sort of amazing – but in a bad way, but also extremely brazen."
PENN STATE COCAINE BUST NETS 14 ARRESTS OVER ALLEGED PLEDGE COKE-CUTTING ‘INDOCTRINATION' RITUALS

Fraternity culture made more news this past week in Madison, Wisconsin, where police said they found roughly 30 partially clothed young men packed inside a sweltering basement, covered in food, condiments and other liquids – with several pledges showing signs of being physically assaulted.
The Madison Police Department said officers were dispatched to the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) house on Wednesday night and are investigating the hazing incident, with two people arrested.
Partially clothed young men are seen inside the basement of an Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity house in Madison, Wisconsin, during an alleged hazing incident. (Madison Police Department)

"AEPi Headquarters takes the allegations involving our Pi Chapter in Madison, Wisconsin, extremely seriously," Jonathan Pierce, the fraternity's chief communications officer, said in a statement. "We will cooperate fully with the authorities investigating this matter."

"Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for. There is no place for it in AEPi," he added. "No exceptions. No excuses. We educate our members about their responsibility to ‘Be Your Brothers’ Keeper.’ This is not an optional value."
‘Sad moment’

"It's a sad moment, for society, civilization," Lohse said about some of the recent headlines involving fraternity behavior. "These organizations should be forces of good. Young men need it more than ever. Young men are more adrift than ever, there's no moral leadership."
"There's a vacuum in the center of higher education and American society that used to be filled by God, by religion, by the church," he said, adding that it's "totally vacant now."

During his time as a brother at Sigma Alpha Epsilon, he said he was forced to "swim in a kiddie pool full of vomit while being urinated on," and "chug" vinegar or milk to the point that he and his fellow pledge brothers "would vomit" in a room covered with tarps.
FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS
Six men are among fourteen facing charges in the alleged Penn State fraternity coke ring off campus. (Getty Images: GRICHKA BEYSSON-LEANDRI; Pennsylvania OAG)
He also said he was forced into a small basement crawl space for a period of time. This was all in addition to constant coerced binge drinking, he said.
"We're talking like 10, 15 plus drinks," he said.
MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY
He said the unwritten "code of silence" or "omertà" contributes to these repeated hazing or drug-related issues within frats.
"The original 19th-century concept of the American fraternity is not what exists today," Lohse said.
THREE COLLEGE FRATS IN CROSSHAIRS AS HAZING CLAIMS OF BOOZE, BURNS AND HOSPITAL TRIPS SPARK CRACKDOWN: SCHOOL

Agostino Abbatiello arrives at Centre County Courthouse in Bellefonte, Pa., Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. Abbatiello is accused of masterminding a cocaine ring at Penn State University. (Kamil Krzaczynski for Fox News Digital)

"Essentially, you can look at a modern fraternity like a criminal organization. In most states, the unique behavioral attributes of a fraternity cross into criminal statutes—whether misdemeanor hazing or serious felony drug trafficking. You need a code of silence to protect that."
He went on to say, "the organization forces the individual to compromise their own identity for the collective, taking something from its members to ensure the system perpetuates itself over time."
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Following the hazing incidents during Lohse's time as a student, SAE was suspended from Dartmouth for the last 10 years and re-recognized in August, The Darmouth student-run paper reported.

When asked what advice he would offer students considering Greek life at major universities, Lohse stopped short of telling students flatly to avoid fraternities. Instead, Lohse urges young men to calculate the "opportunity cost" before pledging.
"Consider that the upside benefit, while maybe not zero, pales in comparison to the downside risk," Lohse said, advising incoming students to reflect on what they truly want out of higher education.
SEND US A TIP
The College Green on the campus of Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire, U.S., on Sunday, Oct. 17, 2021. (Bing Guan/Bloomberg)
GOT A TIP?

"Think about what you actually want out of college. Who do you really want to be around, and who is actually going to be there to help you? I think you'll find that a fraternity isn't going to provide that."

Judson Horras, president and CEO of the North American Interfraternity Conference, told Fox News Digital that "student safety is our members' highest priority. The NIC has adopted enhanced health and safety guidelines and co-led advocacy to pass tougher anti-hazing laws in more than a dozen states, as well as the federal Stop Campus Hazing Act."

Regarding the Ole Miss students' deaths, Horras said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of two University of Mississippi students, one of whom was a fraternity member. Our sympathies are with both families and the Ole Miss community. We will continue working with universities and families to keep every student safe."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Sigma Alpha Epsilon, Phi Delta Theta and Abbatiello's attorney for comment.

title: Family of paralyzed Marine vet allegedly shot by migrant speaks out as health issue could delay testimony
summary: Jimmy Friesenhahn, a Marine veteran paralyzed in a San Antonio shooting, faces a health crisis before trial, his family told Fox News Digital.
story: The family of Jimmy Friesenhahn has criticized trial delays and outlined the brutal daily reality of his life-altering injuries.

A Marine veteran left paralyzed after being shot while working as a security guard was slated to testify against his alleged illegal immigrant attacker in court next week until a sudden, severe downturn in his health forced him back into the hospital, his family told Fox News Digital.

Jimmy Friesenhahn, a combat veteran with multiple overseas deployments, has been hospitalized for at least a week due to complications from a blood clot after an August surgery, according to his sister, Becky Borjon.

"We encountered some medical setbacks, and he's been hospitalized for a week now," Borjon said. "Prior to that, he was in inpatient rehab for three weeks following a surgery he had on Aug. 28, and things just kind of took a turn."
ICE RAMPS UP ARRESTS OF CONVICTED CRIMINALS AS RIOTS RAGE IN BLUE CITY: ‘YOU WILL NOT STOP US’
Marine Corps veteran Jimmy Friesenhahn was allegedly shot by an illegal migrant in May. (Credit: GoFundMe)
Friesenhahn was expected to take the stand in a Bexar County courtroom during the upcoming trial of Wilmer Vladimir Ruiz Ortega, 29, the Honduran national accused of shooting him.

"Trial is scheduled to begin next week on the 20th," Borjon said. "I believe they will start with jury selection and go from there. Jimmy was expected to appear and testify on his own behalf, and we are still hoping he will be able to do that."

Ortega was arrested after allegedly shooting Friesenhahn at El Patio Sports Bar in San Antonio May 4, 2025. Police said Friesenhahn spotted a gun in Ortega’s pocket and tried to stop him from entering the venue. A struggle ensued, during which Ortega allegedly fired multiple rounds.
Friesenhahn was struck twice in his bulletproof vest and once in the neck. The wound to his neck left him paralyzed, unable to speak and in need of full-time medical care.
ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WITH LENGTHY RAP SHEET AFTER ALLEGED JEALOUSY-FUELED KILLING
The arrest record of Wilmer Vladimir Ruiz Ortega, a 29-year-old illegal immigrant who allegedly shot a Marine veteran. (Fox News/America Reports)
Ortega was charged with aggravated assault against a security officer and illegal entry into the United States. He is also the subject of federal immigration proceedings.

The shooting sparked outrage from Friesenhahn’s family, who pointed to Ortega’s extensive prior criminal record in Texas. Court records show Ortega was arrested for driving while intoxicated in October 2020, followed by an August 2023 arrest for a probation violation.
He was arrested two more times for failing to appear in court, including a November 2024 arrest.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS
Becky Borjon and Emmanuel Martinez   (Fox News/America Reports)

"His last court appearance was in March 2025, and Jimmy was shot on May 4, 2025," said Emmanuel Martinez, Friesenhahn’s brother-in-law. "At that point, the DA’s office should have complied with removal orders and turned him over to Immigration and Customs Enforcement."
Borjon echoed those concerns, questioning why Ortega remained free despite repeated offenses.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF FENTANYL DEALING LINKED TO VIRGINIA HIGH SCHOOL OVERDOSES

"I’m not opposed to immigration, but there is a process set in place for a reason," Borjon said. "This guy was arrested multiple times, released on bond and never reported. He had active warrants for repeated offenses while missing court appearances.
"Those warrants should have been acted upon, and maybe we wouldn’t be here today. This guy should have been returned to his country."
Friesenhahn’s family remains determined to see the case prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law, while coming to terms with the reality of his life-altering injuries.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Unfortunately, we don’t see this as a road to recovery because there is no recovering from an injury like this. We see it as the beginning of a lifelong fight," Borjon said. "My brother will never walk again. He will never be able to get married or raise a family."
The Bexar County District Attorney's Office declined to comment to Fox News Digital on the status of the case.

title: Review of Charlie Kirk's assassination at Utah Valley University made public
summary: A 158-page report reveals UVU security was insufficient for Charlie Kirk's outdoor event with inconsistent policies and no camera monitoring.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Claudia Cowan has details on the wrongful death legal warning filed by Charlie Kirk's family against Utah Valley University on ‘Special Report.’

Utah Valley University has released a 158-page report into the circumstances surrounding the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk on campus last year, when he was shot and killed during a public speaking event in the school's central courtyard.

The report, conducted independently by the Lake Forest Group but commissioned and released by the school, identified 10 "key findings" aimed at improving security for future events and concluded that no one at UVU acted "in bad faith or in willful and wanton disregard for the safety of others."

Among those key takeaways, the reviewers found that UVU's application of its own policies "was significantly inconsistent;" security was insufficient for a high-profile, outdoor event and there was no one in the university police department assigned to monitor campus security cameras.
CHARLIE KIRK'S FAMILY ALLEGES UVU KNEW OF ROOFTOP SECURITY RISK BEFORE HIS ASSASSINATION: LEGAL FILING

Charlie Kirk appears at Utah Valley University Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking on his American Comeback Tour when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
The reviewers also recommended reevaluating staffing levels and training given the university's size and potential for risk.
KIRK FAMILY MAY HAVE PATH AROUND ARCHAIC LAW SHIELDING GOV'T IN POLICE CHIEF'S ALLEGED 'GOT YOU COVERED' TEXT
Read the full report:

One concern raised in the report is that while universities have established systems to identify and thwart internal threats since the 2007 Virginia Tech shooting, those measures weren't applicable in the Kirk case because accused assassin Tyler Robinson had no connection to the school.

The report also concluded a timeline of major events in the lead-up to Kirk's visit to UVU between July 10 and Sept. 9, 2025. Several "key decision points" were identified between Aug. 25 and the day of Kirk's murder on Sept. 10.
SURVEILLANCE VIDEO TIMELINE TRACKS ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN ACROSS UVU CAMPUS BEFORE FATAL ROOFTOP SHOT

The view after shots were fired at an appearance by Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking on his American Comeback Tour when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

On Aug. 25, the outdoor courtyard location remained the event venue despite concerns from UVU officials about their ability to control it, according to the review. Two days later, the event was approved without a documented security assessment plan in place. Campus police and TPUSA security had their "first direct security coordination" on Sept. 3, a week before the event.

On Sept. 8, TPUSA organizers raised their concerns about rooftop access in the area above where Kirk would be speaking. The report states that UVU Police Chief Jeffrey Long sent TPUSA security supervisor Dan Flood a text stating, "We got you covered," but the review claims that the text was "in reference to the Hall of Flags outdoor pedestrian walkway."
Flood arrived in person on campus on Sept. 10 with the TPUSA security team.

Law enforcement tapes off an area after Charlie Kirk, the CEO and co-founder of the conservative youth organization Turning Point USA, was shot at the Utah Valley University Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. (Tess Crowley/The Deseret News via AP)

"Dan Flood, TPUSA Security Supervisor, texted Chief Long advising that TPUSA security personnel had arrived on campus," the report states. "Chief Long engaged in a series of text communications with Flood, to include several regarding individuals located on the Hall of Flags outdoor pedestrian walkway and the Fountain Courtyard area where a canopy would be set up where Kirk would be speaking. These text exchanges revealed the primary security focus for TPUSA was the Hall of Flags outdoor pedestrian walkway above the canopy."

This account differs from language in the Kirk family's notice of claim against UVU, filed last week, which identified the Sorensen Center rooftop as an area of concern, not the Hall of Flags walkway.
The Hall of Flags walkway was closed for the event, but TPUSA security never met with university police in person, according to the review.
CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION: NEW UVU PRESIDENT SAYS IT WILL CONTINUE TO 'HOST THE FRAYS,' EMBRACE FREE SPEECH
Ultimately, prosecutors allege that Robinson climbed atop the Losee Center building, which is to the northeast of the courtyard, and fired the fatal shot from there.
The Hall of Flags walkway is directly above where Kirk was speaking. The Sorenson Center is the building to the north. The Losee Center is to the northeast.
ALLEGED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON'S FINGERPRINTS, PALM PRINT FOUND NEAR ROOFTOP: REPORT
A map of the UVU campus shows key locations surrounding the courtyard where Charlie Kirk was shot and killed Sept. 10, 2025. (After-Action report for Utah Valley University)

"This report reaffirms the facts we laid out in our Notice of Claim: that UVU security was woefully understaffed and unprepared to manage the obvious risks associated with an event of this nature," Kirk family attorney Brett Parkinson said in a statement to Fox News Digital Friday.
"UVU hosted this event, and in doing so, assumed responsibility for the safety of all in attendance, including Charlie."
SEND US A TIP

As the family alleged last week, University Police Chief Jeffrey Long allegedly told Turning Point USA organizers that "I got you covered" when they raised concerns about rooftop access above the courtyard where Kirk was ultimately shot and killed by a sniper.
HOW CHARLIE KIRK’S ASSASSINATION CHANGED THE WAY CONSERVATIVES APPROACH HOSTILE OPPONENTS

Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina of the Utah Department of Public Safety, motions toward a map of the Utah Valley University campus during a preliminary hearing for Tyler Robinson, who is accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, at the Fourth District Courthouse in Provo, Utah, July 9, 2026 (Spenser Heaps/AP via Pool)
"The buck stopped with UVU leadership and law enforcement," Parkinson said. "Justice for Charlie and his family requires true accountability for UVU’s fatal shortcomings that day."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
A university spokesperson told Fox News the school has no further comment beyond a statement released on behalf of UVU President Jon Anderson.
Tyler Robinson, accused of the murder of Charlie Kirk, appears during a hearing in Fourth District Court in Provo, Utah, Dec. 11, 2025. (Rick Egan/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)

"September 10 will always be part of UVU’s history, but it will not define our future," he said. "Our responsibility is to care for our community, learn from the findings of this review and follow through on its recommendations. This requires humility, an honest examination of our policies and practices and a commitment to act on what we learn."

title: Ole Miss toxicology reports expected soon and results may trigger anti-fentanyl law, official says
summary: Toxicology reports in the Ole Miss deaths of Robert Strang and Aidan Hamilton could come within days as investigators weigh kratom and foul play.
story: Fox News correspondent Madison Scarpino reports on the deaths of University of Mississippi students Aiden Hamilton and Robert Strang in Oxford, Mississippi. Scarpino details authorities’ efforts to expedite toxicology reports as investigators examine the circumstances surrounding the deaths on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

OXFORD, Miss. — Toxicology reports in the suspicious deaths of two University of Mississippi students are expected to be completed as early as next week, according to the state's commissioner of public safety, and Oxford police have separately announced arrests in connection with a raid on a tobacco shop accused of trafficking narcotics.

The victims have been identified as Robert Strang, a 20-year-old junior from Atlanta, and Aidan Hamilton, an 18-year-old freshman from Colorado. Both families have asked for privacy and compassion as they mourn the loss of their sons.

It remains unclear how the students died, but narcotics detectives are involved in investigations into both of their deaths. If the reports find fentanyl, there is a special Mississippi law that can be used to target whoever sold it, according to authorities.

"Under Parker’s Law, enacted in 2022, criminal charges may be pursued when an unlawful delivery of fentanyl results in a person’s death," Sean Tindell, the commissioner of Mississippi's Department of Public Safety, told Fox News Digital. "If the investigation establishes those circumstances, law enforcement will work with prosecutors to pursue the appropriate charges and hold those responsible accountable."
OLE MISS DEATHS, DRUGGINGS HAVE ‘PEOPLE SCARED TO LEAVE’ DORMS AS BARS, GREEK LIFE CLAMP DOWN: STUDENTS

Aidan Hamilton, an 18-year-old University of Mississippi freshman, appears in these images that his mother posted to Facebook. He is one of two Ole Miss students who died under suspicious circumstances this week. (Facebook/ Kathie Mac Donald Hamilton)

Separately, Oxford police have announced the arrests of two men in a narcotics investigation connected to a local tobacco shop. It's not immediately clear whether the raid has any connection to the student deaths.

"At this point in time, we do not know that," Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch told Fox News Digital about whether the arrests are connected to the deaths. "We know that, again, it's been a very thorough situation as they are going through and making these arrests and preparing the evidence. So we don't know at this point if they are connected at all."
WATCH: Mississippi AG says ‘lives at risk’ amid drug investigations

The suspects were linked to an Oxford retail business where police allegedly found stockpiles of drugs including THC products and kratom, which is legal in many parts of the country but not in Lafayette County.

"During the search, agents recovered more than 500 units of kratom, along with an assortment of THC cartridges, gummies, and other suspected narcotics," police said in a statement. "Kratom has been prohibited from possession, distribution, and sale within the City of Oxford since 2019."
SEND US A TIP
The store is called Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store, located in the 100 block of Heritage Drive in Oxford.
General view of Puffs Vape store, Sept. 25, 2026, in Oxford, Mississippi. (Rashid Umar Abassi for Fox News Digital)
Oxford police arrested Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Mohamed, 18. Both are local residents.

In 2022, the business owner, Amer Alowdi, 40, was indicted on narcotics trafficking charges and fled the country before being prosecuted, police said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how the business remained open.
Interior view of Puffs Vape store, Sept. 25, 2026, in Oxford, Mississippi. (Rashid Umar Abassi for Fox News Digital)
Tindell told Fox News Digital Thursday that while authorities haven't uncovered any indications of foul play, they haven't ruled it out either.
"Until the autopsy is reported, and the investigators have an opportunity to get statements and collect evidence, then that final determination will not be made until later," he said.
WHAT IS KRATOM? RISKS OF POPULAR SUBSTANCE REVEALED AFTER COLLEGE STUDENTS' DEATHS
Robert Strang pictured in an undated family photo. The 20-year-old University of Mississippi junior died under suspicious circumstances. (Strang family)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Without the toxicology reports, it's also too early to determine whether kratom or other drugs were involved in the deaths. Police previously said that they found packages of kratom, which is commercially available in many places but not in Lafayette County, at both scenes.

General view of Phi Delta Theta fraternity house on the Campus of the University of Mississippi in Oxford, Mississippi, September 24, 2026. Black ribbons are tied to the columns of the porch in honor of the death of fraternity member, 20-year-old Robert Strang from Atlanta. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)
Classmates have also circulated warnings about a powerful synthetic opioid called cychlorphine, which they say can take multiple doses of Narcan to counteract.

Gov. Tate Reeves pledged to provide state resources this week to help expedite the toxicology reports. They can typically take weeks to complete, but it may boil down to a matter of days in the Ole Miss case.

title: Suspect in Pittsburgh doctor's murder had been released without bail on prior burglary charge: court docs
summary: Dr. Idris Evans was allegedly stabbed to death in his Edgewood, Pennsylvania, home by an intruder his wife says wore only underwear and ranted about God.
story: Allegheny County police have arrested man accused of attacking a Pittsburgh pediatrician and his wife as they slept. Alexis McAdams reports on the criminal homicide investigation and the charges filed against the suspect.
A Pittsburgh pediatrician is dead, and his wife is hospitalized after a home invasion stabbing attack in their Edgewood, Pennsylvania home, according to authorities.

Allegheny County police have arrested 32-year-old Elijah Hemingway, of Pittsburgh. He has a rap sheet in the county courthouse going back to 2016, with his most recent prior arrest coming in July in connection with a burglary that took place in February, according to court records.
He was released without bail on that charge.
PITTSBURGH DOCTOR STABBED TO DEATH AFTER INTRUDER ALLEGEDLY ATTACKS HIM, WIFE AS THEY SLEPT: POLICE

The Evans family pictured in an undated photograph from a GoFundMe campaign launched for their benefit. Dr. Idris Evans, far right, was killed in a home invasion stabbing early Thursday morning. His wife, center, was hospitalized in stable condition. (GoFundMe)
On Thursday, authorities brought seven new charges against him in connection with the attack — including criminal homicide, aggravated assault, burglary and trespassing.

Hemingway is accused of breaking into the victim's home on Linden Avenue around 12:30 a.m., although he allegedly told police that he had been invited inside by Dr. Evans without being able to provide any information about how they'd met. Police found blood on a windowsill and exterior door in the family's kitchen.

Evans' wife, whose name has not been released by police, was hospitalized with stab wounds. According to the affidavit, she escaped the attack and fled to the home of a neighbor, who called 911 at around 12:31 a.m. Thursday. Police arrived in about 3 minutes.

She later told police that Hemingway appeared "psychotic" and claimed to be "God" — while attacking the couple in his underwear. She told police that her husband appeared to address the attacker by name, but she said she'd never seen him before.
The victims were rushed to the hospital as police launched a manhunt for their attacker. Dr. Evans was pronounced dead in the hospital at 1:42 a.m.
A Monroeville Police K-9 named Channy found Hemingway, wearing nothing but underwear, two doors down from the crime scene.

According to the affidavit, he had cuts on his hands consistent with committing a stabbing attack. Hemingway allegedly told police that he had been invited into the home by Dr. Evans — and also claimed that the doctor stabbed him in the back first.
According to court documents, Hemingway "did not have a stab wound on his back" and had no injuries aside from cuts on his hands.

title: Mistress told ‘American Idol’ contestant she wanted ‘to kill’ wife but testified divorce, not murder, was plan
summary: Alleigha Botner testified about Caleb Flynn's eerie remark after Ashley Flynn's death and the final messages exchanged before the shooting.
story: Testimony continues as Flynn stands accused of fatally shooting his wife, Ashley, in February.

Jurors spent hours Thursday listening to droves of messages exchanged between former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn and his former mistress, Alleigha Botner, before defense attorneys sought to recast the relationship as an emotionally volatile affair centered on divorce – not murder.
The day ended with an Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation digital forensics expert beginning testimony about data recovered from Flynn's cellphone.
Here are the biggest moments from Day 6 of testimony:
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)
Botner testified that she and Flynn exchanged messages about wanting his wife dead months before Ashley was killed.
"I just wish I didn't say this," she said as she became emotional on the stand.
Botner then read her message to Flynn: "I want to kill her, Caleb."
She said Flynn responded: "That makes two of us."
WATCH: Caleb Flynn had ominous response when mistress said ‘I want to kill her’
Prosecutors focused heavily on the final hours before Ashley Flynn was shot, walking jurors through messages exchanged the night before her death.
Botner repeatedly questioned whether Flynn was prepared to leave his wife.
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY

"I said, 'Caleb, I've never felt anything as deep as I felt with you. I trusted you with my heart. I'm terrified. But thank you for saying all that. We will see if your actions finally match your words,'" Botner testified, reading from the messages.
She said Flynn responded: "I've never felt anything like it either. It's why I know it's actually real ... I'm terrified as well, but tomorrow it all starts."
WATCH: 'You have murdered my heart': Secret affair messages revealed in Caleb Flynn trial
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY

When Botner asked whether he was "more excited or scared," Flynn allegedly replied: "Well, I got a pretty massive day tomorrow so I'm gonna head to sleep. Please be praying for me and I'll update you the whole time."
Later in the conversation, Botner testified she wrote: "You're about to be free."
MISTRESS SAYS SHE GAVE ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT ULTIMATUM BEFORE WIFE’S KILLING BLEW UP AFFAIR
She said Flynn replied: "I choose you ... You're more than enough. Good night."

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)
Botner testified she later went to Ashley's parents' home, where church staff had gathered after the shooting.
She said Flynn hugged her shortly after she arrived.
"The first thing he said to me was, 'It didn't happen the way we thought it would, did it?'"
She testified she immediately questioned him about what happened and became increasingly suspicious as he described hearing a gunshot, finding blood inside the home and discovering Ashley.
Alleigha Botner wipes away tears while testifying about messages exchanged with Caleb Flynn during his murder trial in Ohio. (CREDIT: WKEF)
Defense attorney Emily Smith sought to reframe the prosecution's key evidence, arguing Botner understood Flynn's messages to be about leaving his wife – not killing her.
Smith asked whether Flynn's repeated references to becoming "free," taking action and leaving Ashley meant he intended to divorce her.

title: Pittsburgh doctor stabbed to death after intruder allegedly attacks him, wife as they slept: police

story: Suspect Elijah Hemingway of Pittsburgh is in custody in connection to the stabbing death of Dr. Idris Evans, whose wife was also injured in the attack as they slept Thursday. (KDKA)

A Pittsburgh children's hospital doctor was stabbed to death and his wife critically injured after a man allegedly entered their home and attacked the couple as they slept early Thursday, police said.
Dr. Idris Evans, 46, was killed in the attack at his home in Edgewood, Pennsylvania, according to the Allegheny County Police Department.
His wife remained in critical but stable condition Thursday, police told Fox News Digital.
County 9-1-1 received a report of a stabbing in the 100 block of Linden Avenue at 12:31 a.m. First responders found Evans and his wife suffering from multiple stab wounds, police said.

Evans was taken to an area hospital, where he was pronounced dead. His wife was also transported to a hospital.
Police identified 32-year-old Elijah Hemingway of Pittsburgh as the suspect.
Detectives determined through witness interviews that Hemingway allegedly entered the home and attacked Evans and his wife while they were sleeping, according to police.

Evans' wife told investigators that they awoke to a man attacking them in bed with a kitchen knife, according to court documents obtained by KDKA. She said the attacker was wearing only underwear and uttered about "being God," the outlet reported.

During the attack, Evans' wife yelled for the couple's children, ages 8 and 12, to get out of the house and go to a neighbor's home, according to KDKA.
She also told investigators that Evans called the attacker "Elijah," as though he knew him, according to the outlet.

"We do not know if there was any pre-existing relationship," Allegheny County Assistant Superintendent Victor Joseph said, according to KDKA. "The woman did not know this male. We are trying to determine if the two males knew each other."

A K-9 unit from the Monroeville Police Department searching the area found Hemingway behind a nearby home with cuts to his hand, according to county police. Hemingway remained hospitalized Thursday pending transfer to the Allegheny County Jail, police told Fox News Digital.
Hemingway faces charges including criminal homicide, aggravated assault, burglary and criminal trespass, police said. Police told Fox News Digital there were no updates to the charges Thursday.
NORTH CAROLINA MAN BROKE INTO EX'S HOME, FATALLY STABBED HIS 5-YEAR-OLD SON BEFORE GOING TO TACO BELL: POLICE

A Pittsburgh children's hospital doctor was stabbed to death and his wife critically injured after a man allegedly entered their home and attacked the couple. (Robert Knopes/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)
Investigators have not announced a motive. Police told Fox News Digital that both a possible motive and whether Hemingway and Evans knew each other remained part of the ongoing investigation.

Evans was the medical director of the Pediatric Critical Care Transport Team at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh and an assistant professor of critical care medicine at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, according to his university profile.

"Dr. Evans was a dedicated caregiver and valued member of our hospital and university communities. Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this difficult time. We ask that their privacy be respected."

A nurse is accused of beating a prematurely born 4-month-old baby girl at a Michigan hospital, leaving the infant with broken bones and bruises, including injuries to her tongue, according to reports.
Kieran Ansley, 43, who was fired from Helen DeVos Children’s Hospital in Grand Rapids, is charged with multiple counts of child abuse.
The child was born four months premature but was making progress after spending months in the ICU and was expected to go home in April, WOOD-TV reported.
TEXAS DENTIST ACCUSED OF FATAL MISTAKES AFTER 4-YEAR-OLD DIES DURING DENTAL PROCEDURE
Kieran Ansley, a former nurse, allegedly abused a 4-month-olf girl born prematurely while the infant was recovering in a hospital. (Kent County jail; Google Maps)

The girl's mother visited her April 2. As she approached the room, Ansley "‘jogged’ to cut them off before getting to the room, telling them that the infant had ‘slept through the night,’" court records show.

Others recalled Ansley being "heated" and "overwhelmed," court records show.

A staff log from the night the infant was allegedly abused showed 32 instances in which someone entered the baby’s room. Ansley accounted for 27 of those visits, the records show, the news station reported.
Fox News Digital reached out to Ansley's attorney and the hospital for comment.
Defense attorney Damian Nunzio told the news outlet Ansley has been cooperative during the investigation, spent "many years" working with ICU patients and is a "very good person.
"And we are confident that our investigation will let the truth come to light," Nunzio added.
Ansley, who was released on bond and is expected to appear in court Nov. 10, was fired after the allegations came to light.
The child, now 10 months old, is at home and "doing wonderful," Steavens said.

title: Angel mom says blue state DAs are putting illegal immigrant criminals before public safety
summary: Cheryl Minter's Change.org petition targets Fairfax County prosecutor Steve Descano after her daughter's accused killer had over 30 prior arrests.
story: Cheryl Minter calls for Virginia prosecutor Steve Descano’s removal after an illegal immigrant with more than 30 prior arrests was charged in her daughter Stephanie’s bus stop killing.

A Virginia mother whose daughter was stabbed to death at a bus stop is fighting to oust the county's top prosecutor after learning the accused killer had been arrested more than 30 times before the attack.

"Stephanie should be alive today," Cheryl Minter wrote in a petition calling for Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano to be removed. "I had to do what no parent should ever have to. I had to bury my daughter."

Stephanie Minter, 41, was found with multiple stab wounds inside a bus stop shelter in Hybla Valley Feb. 23, Fairfax County police said. Abdul Jalloh, 32, was charged with second-degree murder. He has not been convicted in her death.
"She was an amazingly strong woman, amazingly strong, and happy and brought brightness and joy to so many people," Cheryl Minter told Fox News Digital.
SOROS-BACKED DA'S LAX ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION POLICIES LED TO 'PREVENTABLE' BUS STOP STABBING MURDER: COMPLAINT
Abdul Jalloh, 32, is accused of killing Stephanie Minter, 41, at a bus stop in Virginia. (Fox 5 DC)

The Department of Homeland Security says Jalloh, a Sierra Leone national who entered the U.S. illegally in 2012, has been arrested more than 30 times. His previous charges included rape, malicious wounding, assault and theft, DHS said.
SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW
"I was shocked. I mean, literally in shock," Cheryl Minter said when asked about his record. "And then this man who's killed her, just is let off like it's nothing. Like it's nothing."
In her petition, Cheryl Minter blamed Descano's decisions for what she called a preventable death.
"Thirty times the system had a chance to stop him. Thirty times," she wrote. "I think about that every single day."
JORDAN GRILLS SOROS-BACKED DA DESCANO IN HEATED SPAT OVER SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICY: 'THIS IS ALMOST LAUGHABLE'

Cheryl questioned why Jalloh was released after an arrest she recalled from the winter before Stephanie's death. The details of that case and who made the release decision have not been independently confirmed.
"When you let these people back out on the streets, they're not gonna stop. Why would they stop?" she said.

Cheryl Minter also pointed to Descano's 2020 plea bargaining policy. It advised prosecutors to "consider immigration consequences where possible" and weigh how charges could affect a defendant's immigration status, WTOP reported. The outlet reported in May that the webpage detailing the policy was no longer publicly available on Descano's office website. Cheryl Minter argues that prosecutors should put public safety first.

That policy is under federal scrutiny. The Justice Department announced in May it was investigating whether Descano's office gave defendants who are in the country illegally preferential treatment over U.S. citizens in charging decisions and plea deals. The department said it had reached no conclusions. The investigation does not establish how Jalloh's earlier cases were handled.
SOROS-BACKED PROSECUTOR SET FOR CAPITOL HILL GRILLING AS SANCTUARY POLICIES FACE RECKONING
Descano defended the policy after receiving notice of the investigation.
"My policies are fair, legal, and reflect the values of my community," he wrote in a post on X.
Asked what she wants from her petition, Cheryl Minter said her priority is changing those practices in Fairfax County and beyond. She also wants Descano out of office.
SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP
Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Stephen Descano, center, listens to testimony during a hearing before a House Judiciary Subcommittee. (Tom Williams/CQ via Getty Images)
"I think, first and foremost, is the change," she said. "Second would be, I would love to see Descano out."

Jennifer Harrison, executive director of the Victims' Rights Reform Council, helped Cheryl Minter start the Change.org petition. Cheryl Minter said she knows an online petition cannot itself remove Descano but hopes it will drive scrutiny of his office.

Congress is also pressing Descano for answers. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, subpoenaed him Sept. 16 as part of an investigation into whether prosecutors give preferential treatment to criminal suspects because of their immigration status.
Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, during a hearing with the House Judiciary Committee in the Rayburn House Office Building on Sept. 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
Jordan set a Sept. 25 deadline after accusing Descano's office of failing to fully comply with earlier requests.

In a previous statement to Fox News Digital, Descano's office called the subpoena a "needless escalation" and accused the committee of waging a "partisan siege" against Fairfax County. It said the office had turned over more than 1,100 pages of documents, that Descano had voluntarily testified and that it would continue to respond to legitimate inquiries while working to keep the county safe.
The office has separately said it is prosecuting Jalloh for Stephanie's murder with a trial scheduled for January 2027 and cannot comment further on the pending case.
WATCH: SOROS PROSECUTOR’S HEARING DEVOLVES INTO ANGRY CHAOS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RAPE CASE: 'BE QUIET!'
Fairfax County police said Jalloh was arrested after an employee at a local business recognized him and called authorities the day after Stephanie Minter was killed. He was held without bond.

ICE lodged a detainer on Feb. 25 after Jalloh was in custody, asking to be notified before his release, according to DHS. The agency said it had also lodged a detainer against him in 2020 and that an immigration judge later ordered him removed to a country other than Sierra Leone.

Cheryl Minter said employees of Descano's office working on her daughter's murder case have been "wonderful with me." She said her criticism is aimed at the decisions she believes left a repeat offender free.
"I want people never to stop talking about it," she said. "I just don't want the talk to stop, and I'll do whatever to keep it going."

"Stephanie cannot speak for herself anymore. So I am," she wrote in the petition.

title: Hayden Panettiere's overdose shows fentanyl crisis 'doesn't discriminate,' Stanford psychiatrist says
summary: Hayden Panettiere's fatal fentanyl overdose involved a lethal mix of opioids, benzodiazepines and quetiapine, a Stanford addiction expert says.
story: In the wake of Hayden Panettiere's accidental overdose, Stanford addiction medicine specialist Dr. Anna Lembke explains fentanyl's dangers, the risks of mixing medications and why today's drug supply is more dangerous than ever.
Hayden Panettiere's fatal overdose is a stark reminder that the fentanyl crisis has not gone away, even as the United States makes genuine progress in reducing overdose deaths since peaking in 2022.
This week, the Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled that Panettiere died from the toxic effects of five drugs found in her system: fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine.

Dr. Anna Lembke, a Stanford psychiatrist and addiction medicine specialist, told Fox News Digital that while the circumstances surrounding the actress' death remain unclear, the combination of drugs in her system likely increased the risk of a fatal overdose.

"We don't know if she sought out fentanyl. We don't know if she had a counterfeit pill that had fentanyl in it. She might have been prescribed fentanyl for pain," Lembke said. "She was also on a benzo. We know combining benzos and opioids increases the risk of overdose of each of those medications separately. It looks like she was also on Quetiapine, a mood stabilizer, but also highly sedating in the mix."
Hayden Panettiere discusses "Nashville" with the Build Series at AOL HQ on Jan. 5, 2017, in New York City. (Roy Rochlin/FilmMagic)
HAYDEN PANETTIERE DEATH: DEA JOINS PROBE INTO WHAT HAPPENED TO LATE STAR
Lembke continued: "We don't know where she sourced it, but it does look like it was a lethal polypharmacy, including fentanyl, which on its own is an incredibly lethal drug."
The Cleveland Clinic defines polypharmacy as taking several medicines regularly, usually four or more.

While Lembke cautioned against drawing firm conclusions about what exactly led up to Panettiere's death, she said the tragedy underscores a broader reality: fentanyl remains a deadly threat that can affect anyone.

"This is still a very serious risk, and it's a risk that doesn't discriminate. Old and young, rich and poor, famous, not famous. Because of the increased access to these highly potent and potentially lethal drugs in the modern age, we're really all at risk for this problem," Lembke said.
Fentanyl, a synthetic opioid up to 50 times more potent than heroin, has transformed the nation's illicit drug supply over the past decade.
Pills containing fentanyl are displayed at the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Northeast Regional Laboratory for testing in New York, on May 7, 2026. (Angela Weiss/AFP via Getty Images)
PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY
Deaths involving synthetic opioids, primarily illicitly manufactured fentanyl, began climbing sharply in 2014 and reached a record 73,838 in 2022, according to the National Institute on Drug Abuse.

Fentanyl's potency is only part of what makes it so dangerous, Lembke said. Just as concerning is how trace amounts are concealed in counterfeit pills designed to look like legitimate prescription medications.

Lembke said a "very real risk" for young people, even those who aren't struggling with addiction, is that they're given a pill at a party that looks just like Xanax or Oxycontin, when it is in fact a counterfeit pill that contains a small amount of fentanyl.
"A single dose to an opioid-naive person could kill, which is why it's so important that we have data-informed discussions with young people in particular," she said.
"The kind of experimentation with drugs in their youth that their parents might've engaged in relatively risk-free... it's not risk-free anymore" for young adults, she added.
Anna Lembke, a Stanford psychiatrist and author, gives a lecture on May 19, 2026, in Berlin, Germany. (Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lembke encouraged parents to get ahead of the issue by talking openly about drugs before their children encounter inaccurate or misleading information on social media.
If a parent or guardian recognizes their child has a substance-use disorder, Lembke said they should resist the impulse to brush it off as "normal teenage experimentation."

"These drugs are far too accessible and far too lethal to just leave it to hoping that it will be a passing phase the kid will outgrow," she said. "We know that the earlier we intervene with addiction-related problems, the more likely we are to reroute that person on a new path of life."
Lembke also offered a message to doctors, who she said should prescribe potentially addictive medications cautiously and closely monitor patients for signs of misuse.

As a practicing psychiatrist, Lembke routinely prescribes stimulants for ADHD, opioids for pain and benzodiazepines for insomnia and anxiety. But she said physicians have a responsibility to prescribe them in the lowest effective amounts for the shortest possible duration.

title: Ole Miss names students found dead as official addresses potential for foul play
summary: It remains unclear whether the deaths of Ole Miss students are connected, according to Lafayette County authorities.
story: Editor-in-Chief Regan Settle of Ole Miss's student-run news organization The Daily Mississippian, highlights growing student frustration after two campus drug overdose deaths, pressing university leaders to communicate directly.

OXFORD, Miss. — The two University of Mississippi students found dead under suspicious circumstances in recent days have been identified by the school — which also said the names were being released with their families' approval.
Robert Strang, a 20-year-old from Atlanta, is the older of the two victims. The second student was as Aidan Hamilton, an 18-year-old freshman from Colorado.

"We are heartbroken by the loss of our dear son and are trying to process this unimaginable loss," Strang's family spokesman Scott Sayres told Fox News Digital Thursday. "We are deeply grateful for the incredible outpouring of love, prayers and support by so many beloved friends and family. Their kindness has meant more to our family than we can ever express."

Hamilton's family said in a statement that "Aidan was a bright, wonderful young man who was taken too soon. He is greatly missed. We thank everyone for their prayers and support and ask that you respect our family’s privacy during this time of great loss."
Both families have asked for privacy and compassion as they mourn the losses of their sons.
TWO OLE MISS STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS PACKAGED KRATOM IS RECOVERED AT TWO SITES: OFFICIALS
Robert Strang pictured in an undated family photo. The 20-year-old University of Mississippi junior died under suspicious circumstances. (Strang family)

Separately, Commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety Sean Tindell told Fox News Digital that while authorities haven't uncovered any indications of foul play, they haven't ruled it out either.
"Until the autopsy is reported, and the investigators have an opportunity to get statements and collect evidence, then that final determination will not be made until later," he said.

Without the toxicology reports, it's also too early to determine whether kratom or other drugs were involved in the deaths. Police previously said that they found packages of kratom, which is commercially available in many places but not Lafayette County, at both scenes.

Aidan Hamilton, an 18-year-old University of Mississippi freshman, appears in these images that his mother posted to Facebook. He is one of two Ole Miss students who died under suspicious circumstances this week. (Facebook/ Kathie Mac Donald Hamilton)

He also said that both deaths happened at around the same time, or at least within a few hours, which was also suspicious. However, he said he expects the autopsy reports to give investigators a more specific window.

"The timing of it is suspicious, but I don't know that they have any direct relation other than if they both had ingested the substance from the same source," he said. "Then at some point we would try to track it back to that source and take appropriate action."

Stewart Hall, a dorm building on the University of Mississippi campus where an 18-year-old student is believed to have died on Monday. Dispatch records show first responders arrived within a minute of being sent to the address. (Adam Sabes/Fox News Digital)
Social media posts from the Ole Miss chapter of the Phi Delta Theta fraternity identify Strang as one of seven co-chairmen of the 2026 Rush, when new members are recruited.

"As our university community continues to mourn the recent tragic loss of two of our students, I encourage everyone to remember that at the center of this are two grieving families, who are processing the unimaginable loss of a child," the school's Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs Dr. Shawnboda Mead said in a statement Thursday afternoon.

"We have been in touch with the families to offer our deepest sympathies and share university support and resources. Until now, we have upheld their wishes not to release the names of their students," she continued. "Today, the families of Aidan Hamilton, a freshman from Englewood, Colo., and Robert Strang, a junior from Atlanta, have given us permission to share their names. The families have asked for privacy as they grieve."
Mead continued to urge the public not to rely on speculation or unverified information about the case as law enforcement continues to investigate both deaths.

"We offer heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and classmates of Aidan and Robert," she said. "While there are no words that can alleviate the tremendous sorrow they are experiencing, please keep them close in your thoughts and prayers during this time of immense grief."
Phi Delta Theta's Ole Miss chapter also put out a statement after the university, asking for prayers for both victims.

"Phi Delta Theta joins the University of Mississippi and the broader Ole Miss community in mourning Robert and Aidan Hamilton and extending our deepest sympathies to their families, friends, chapter brothers, classmates, and all those who knew and loved them."
General view of Stewart Hall, Oxford, MS, September 24, 2026.  (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
Strang was discovered at an off-campus home, according to the Lafayette County Coroner's Office. Hamilton, 18, is believed to have been found at Stewart Hall, a male dorm on the Ole Miss campus.
OLE MISS DEATHS, DRUGGINGS HAVE 'EPOPLE SCARED TO LEAVE' DORMS AS BARS, GREEK LIFE CLAMP DOWN

The Lafayette County Coroner's Office previously told Fox News that an 18-year-old had been found in a dorm room and the 20-year-old victim was recovered at an off-campus home. Both deaths are being investigated by the county's narcotics task force, and it's unclear whether they were connected.
SEND US A TIP

Authorities found packages of kratom, a commercially available drug that has been derided as "gas station heroin," at both scenes, however its role in either death was not immediately clear. Campus Greek life leaders have previously circulated a warning about a synthetic opioid called cychlorphine.
MANHATTAN PROSTITUTE PLEADS GUILTY TO KILLING 3 MEN WITH FENTANYL-LACED DRUGS IN ROBBERY SCHEME
Cychlorphine can be treated with Narcan but sometimes requires multiple doses, students were told. It also may not show up on common drug-detecting strips used to find fentanyl contamination.
Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves gestures and speaks during the Neshoba County Fair in Philadelphia, Miss., on Thursday, June 25, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Students are being urged to avoid all drugs.
CHINESE NATIONALS ACCUSED OF SMUGGLING SYNTHETIC DRUGS INTO US PRISONS ON DRUG-SOAKED PAPER

Gov. Tate Reeves said Wednesday that state investigators were assisting local authorities, and that they would try and expedite the toxicology reports on both victims. Such reports typically take weeks to complete.

title: Texas triple murderer uses last words before execution to send message to death row inmates
summary: Ker'Sean Ramey received lethal injection at Huntsville prison, one week after accomplice LeJames Norman was executed for the same triple killing.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A man convicted of murdering three people in their apartment while searching for drugs to steal was executed in Texas on Wednesday evening, a week after his accomplice was put to death for the same killings.
Ker'Sean Ramey, 41, died by lethal injection at the state penitentiary in Huntsville and was pronounced dead at 6:34 p.m. CDT, The Associated Press reported.
In the execution chamber, a prison chaplain rested his hand on Ramey's shoulder before leading him in a brief prayer. The warden then asked Ramey if he had any last words, the AP reported.
Ramey praised God and thanked his friends, family and fellow death row inmates, whom he called his brothers.
This photo provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice shows Ker'Sean Ramey on Oct. 31, 2022. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice via AP)
ARIZONA EXECUTES MAN WHO KILLED VICTIM BY DOUSING HIM IN GASOLINE AND SETTING HIM ON FIRE IN 2002 ATTACK

"To the brothers on Texas death row that grew up with me, that poured into me and showed what it means to be a man, because I came in young, and didn’t understand what manhood was... to you brothers... I greatly appreciate you," Ramey said moments before the injection was prepared.
As the pentobarbital took effect, Ramey took a deep breath, sputtered and began snoring. After 10 loud snores and two that were barely audible, he went still.
He was pronounced dead 14 minutes after the injection was first administered.
Ramey became the sixth inmate executed in Texas this year, with the state set to carry out three more lethal injections over the next two months.

In January 2007, Ramey was convicted and sentenced to death for the August 2005 shootings of Samuel Roberts, 24, Tiffani Peacock, 18, and Celso Lopez, 38, at a home they shared in Edna, a small rural city about 100 miles southwest of Houston.
The state of Texas execution chamber in Huntsville, Texas, is seen on May 27, 2008. (AP Photo/Pat Sullivan)
74-YEAR-OLD BECOMES FLORIDA'S OLDEST INMATE EXECUTED AFTER 1982 KILLING OF TEEN
LeJames Norman, Ramey's accomplice, lived across the street from the house and the two came to believe there was cocaine there, according to court records.
On Aug. 24, 2005, the men walked over to the home while wearing masks and knocked on the door. After Lopez answered the door, they forced their way inside, records show.

After finding no drugs, the two men fatally shot Lopez, then killed Peacock and Roberts when they arrived at the home. Before fleeing for good, Ramey returned and shot the victims again to ensure they were dead, according to court documents.
Norman was executed on Sept. 16 at the Huntsville prison, where all executions are carried out in Texas.
The Huntsville Unit prison is seen in Huntsville, Texas, on Sept. 14, 2024. (Francois Picard/AFP)
MANHATTAN PROSTITUTE PLEADS GUILTY TO KILLING 3 MEN WITH FENTANYL-LACED DRUGS IN ROBBERY SCHEME

Hours before Ramey was put to death, the Supreme Court rejected his final appeal. Ramey's attorneys argued jurors never heard mitigating evidence about his upbringing, including that he endured physical abuse as a child and grew up in poverty.
State prosecutors urged the Supreme Court to reject the appeal, calling it "meritless" and arguing the record showed Ramey had exhibited an escalating pattern of criminal behavior.

Norman was arrested about five months after the killings while attempting to re-enter the United States from Mexico, where he had fled. During Ramey's January 2007 trial, Norman testified that both men took part in the shootings, while Ramey's attorneys argued Norman was solely responsible.
This photo provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice shows LeJames Norman on Feb. 28, 2024. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice via AP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Ramey's former girlfriend testified that she was with him when he threw two handguns into a lake after the killings and that he later gave her a detailed account of his role in the crime.
Norman pleaded guilty to capital murder and was sentenced to death in December 2008.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Mistress says she gave ‘American Idol’ contestant ultimatum before wife’s killing blew up affair
summary: Caleb Flynn's mistress testified he talked about wanting Ashley Flynn dead and once said he was thinking about ways to kill her before the shooting.
story: Alleigha Botner, ex-mistress of former 'American Idol' contestant Caleb Flynn, delivers emotional testimony during his murder trial. Fox News' Garrett Tenney reports the latest and Fox News contributor Paul Mauro provides his analysis.

Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn told his mistress he stayed up until 4 a.m. "literally thinking of ways to kill" his wife and "not go to jail," one of a series of messages read to jurors Thursday in his Ohio murder trial.
Alleigha Botner returned to the witness stand for a second day and walked jurors through months of messages in which Flynn allegedly talked repeatedly about wanting Ashley Flynn dead or gone.
In one May 2025 message, Flynn allegedly wrote, "If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat."
TEACHER FOUND DEAD WITH THROAT SLIT; DETECTIVES SCRUTINIZE HUSBAND’S SHIFTING STORY
Days later, he allegedly wrote, "I hate her, loathe her. I want her dead."

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)
The messages became even more explicit in June, when Flynn allegedly told Botner, "Please hire someone to take [her] out. I need you in my life, I need you."
Botner responded: "So tempting. I can't live without you. And I've had this thought so often lately. How do we figure this out?"
TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL
Botner later became emotional before reading one of her own messages aloud.
"I want to kill her, Caleb," Botner wrote.

Alleigha Botner testifies Wednesday in the Ohio murder trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn. Prosecutors say Botner had an affair with Flynn before his wife, Ashley Flynn, was killed. (CREDIT: WKEF)
Flynn allegedly responded: "That makes two of us."

Flynn is accused of fatally shooting Ashley in the back of the head inside their home Feb. 16 before staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in. He has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges.
Botner had prefaced the message by telling jurors, "I just wish I didn't say this."
In the same August exchange, Flynn allegedly went on to write that he had been "literally trying to find a way to get rid of her, to be rid of her."
Botner responded that she was "not asking that you take her life, obviously," but said getting a divorce "would change everything."
OHIO MAN CONVICTED AFTER TRYING TO SHOOT EX-WIFE AT POINT-BLANK RANGE INSIDE RESTAURANT IN CHILLING VIDEO

Botner also testified Flynn once showed her a gun he kept in the center console of his truck, though she could not remember what it looked like. Investigators have never recovered the weapon prosecutors allege Flynn used to kill Ashley.
Caleb Flynn in a 2013 "American Idol" Hometown Interview. Caleb is the husband of Ashley Flynn, who was shot and killed in her Ohio home on Monday, February 16, 2026. (YouTube/American Idol)
Jurors also heard that Flynn and Botner routinely deleted messages throughout their relationship.
MICROSOFT EXEC'S GRIEVING WIDOW FACES MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING HIS MURDER AS SHE REVEALS EERIE FINAL CALL
Asked when she advised Flynn how to delete data from his devices, Botner responded, "Multiple times."
"One of them being the night before Ashley was murdered," she testified.
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)

Botner also testified that on the night before Ashley's killing, she used ChatGPT to research whether messages documenting the affair could be permanently deleted and sent Flynn screenshots of the results.

She told jurors she feared the affair could surface during a divorce and cost her her job. Prosecutors established that Botner sent the screenshots about 5:47 p.m. Feb. 15, hours before Ashley was killed.
CALIFORNIA MOM BEGGED FOR HELP BEFORE EX GUNNED HER DOWN IN FRONT OF THEIR 4-YEAR-OLD SON: DA
Caleb and Ashley Flynn are pictured in an undated photo. (Ashley Flynn/Facebook)
SPURNED SPOUSES CASH IN AS NORTH CAROLINA’S 'HOMEWRECKER' LAW TURNS CHEATING INTO A COURTROOM JACKPOT
The two exchanged roughly 107,000 messages while routinely deleting their conversations.
By January, Botner testified, she had grown tired of waiting and gave Flynn a final deadline: leave Ashley by Jan. 11, or she would move on with her life and end their relationship.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Flynn did not leave, and Botner stopped communicating with him until Feb. 14 – Valentine's Day and two days before Ashley was killed.
Ashley Flynn, a Tipp City Schools substitute teacher and volleyball coach, was found dead in her Ohio home. (Tipp City Schools)
That day, she testified, Flynn told her he was "filing [for divorce] from Ashley" and was "actually leaving her this time."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
The night before Ashley was killed, Flynn and Botner discussed his plans for the following day, including telling family members about the divorce and obtaining a burner phone.
After Botner suggested he get the burner first, Flynn allegedly wrote, "I think I should pay cash for this so it's not in my bank account."
FLORIDA PLASTIC SURGEON ACCUSED OF KILLING ATTORNEY IN HIS OFFICE DEFENDS HIMSELF IN MURDER TRIAL
Shortly after midnight, Flynn allegedly told her, "It's happening, Ilya."
Then came another message: "February 16th day I'll never forget."
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Caleb Flynn, 49, was arraigned in court on Friday, Feb. 20. (Dayton Daily News)
Botner responded, "You're about to be free."
SUSPECT IN MICROSOFT EXECUTIVE JARED BRIDEGAN'S MURDER CONVICTED IN ROADSIDE AMBUSH
Flynn replied, "I choose you."
Botner testified those were the final messages Flynn sent her before she learned Ashley had been killed.
At 7:50 a.m., Botner testified she sent Flynn her burner-phone number and told him to contact her there once he obtained his own burner. She later deleted the message.

Caleb Flynn appears in Miami County Common Pleas Court, Troy, Ohio, Monday, March 30, 2026. Flynn is charged with the murder of his wife, 37-year-old Ashley Flynn who was shot to death in their Tipp City home in February. (Matthew Symons for Fox News Digital)
Botner instead learned of Ashley's death after a fellow church congregant sent her a news story that morning.
"My heart started pounding," Botner testified. "It just seemed like too much of a coincidence that the day he's divorcing her, she's just dead all of a sudden."
Botner then messaged Flynn: "What is going on right now? Were you behind this?"
She testified she later deleted the message.
